First, my failed efforts:
I've been going over this post for the last couple of days, and unfortunately haven't made real headway. John as a voice of Wires led me in a long and convoluted research in trying to compare the things he says with things HOPE/Yasu says in order to see if it was repeated (and thus disprove him being a voice for Wires, rather than HOPE - or just himself). But I don't have anything to show for it, which might be a good thing for your theory about him - so at least there's that.
Now, to the interesting stuff:

Say, isn't "Mysterious Abundance of Chickens" the first and perhaps only three-way confrontation between gods? (maybe even four-way)? I'll post your screenshots again for ease of read:
Presumably HOPE speaking (but the thing about "our youth" throws me off - however "I can fill you with such beautiful things" is very HOPE - I've added a screenshot of Yasu saying something similar), and if it is HOPE he does not want Akira remembering whatever this is.



Pareidolia rambling


Wires being the only one actually doing something (and attention to the fact he's apparently trying to reset the whole thing, but wasn't able to)


And SeKaori causing it


Lastly, what the hell was that all about? Why was Akira almost terminated from looking at chickens? And how was this something that SeKaori knew would happen?



So, in this confrontation we have HOPE definitely not wanting it to happen, possibily Wires as well, Pareidolia being present, and all of this being caused by SeKaori. What memories would have been unlocked by chickens I have no idea though - and why was it so important that everyone interfered (as early as chapter 1)?
And to reiterate minor things, Kaori is green on the outside, but she's also afraid of the color green. All gods are dying, and HOPE is the youngest of them (this might be relevant to figuring out their intent with SeKaori).

From this point forward are somewhat minor things to the previous post, but that I found during the research, and could be relevant:
If you go back to where the trees live, you'll notice that every time that SeKaori speaks the world resets, and in my interpretation this could be Wires resetting it, here's why:



Kaori points out that maybe they can't get to where they need to go because the trees are interfering - and Wires not only is a tree, but Tsuneyo speaks about becoming trees all the time.

However, another good point is that, as we know, Nao-chan wasn't there, she was at chicken alley. The one that felt at ease amid trees was Sekai. And going there was awakening SeKaori, which, again, something was trying to prevent by resetting the world everytime she started speaking. My point is, maybe the map wasn't leading them there at all, but SeKaori made Kaori believe it did so that she could awaken - and the forces that saw through this were trying to prevent it, which seemed to be effective through the constant resets in this event until...



Kaori tells the trees not to interfere, and Wires never holds someone against their will. It's only at this moment that the world stops resetting (further evidence that it was a force trying to interfere) and she's awoken:

Now, about Nao-chan's relation to SeKaori:
So, here's the thing, at the beginning of "where the trees live" we see that Nao-chan was sent by people that thought Akira needed help. And one of those reasons might be to counter SeKaori.



Kaori goes full "there's a thing inside of me" after the forest, and Akira feels Sekai's presence.




And then we are told that Kaori was wrong in how she read the map (or was made to be wrong by SeKaori, that used this opportunity to lead her to the forest with Akira and awaken), the actual map was always leading them to the chicken alley and to Nao-chan.

EDIT: I had this post all typed up before I saw Moonflare's new post. I quoted it below where it's relevant to what I'm talking about.

At the end of Nao's event "Eternity Until," she shows The Old One to Sensei, which is cut off if you replay the event. Before that, though, there's a recitation of the Emily Dickinson poem that gives the event its title, and for some reason this is also cut off in the replay. Full text of the poem is here.

The relevant lines are probably "A hallowed thing — to drop a life / Into the purple well — / Too plummetless — that it return —". This sure sounds to me like Sensei (or someone else) being dropped into the Wishing Well and then coming back. It also could be a connection between the Wishing Well and the color purple (or it could be coincidence since this isn't something that Selebus wrote). We also have another connection between purple and the Wishing Well: Nao-chan's color is purple, and she is apparently the result of a wish:
"Human Females":

"Il Cervo":



How Kaori got a gold star and how/when she made her wish are still a mystery, but if purple is connected to the Wishing Well, the opening scene of "Wither" is probably involved. When she's looking up at the sky when Sensei arrives (and "probably thinking of animals" - might be relevant?) she could be "wishing on a star."

Also unknown is what exactly her wish was (I doubt it was for a weird spirit child with mismatched eyes and no ability to talk). I think it was Moonflare who suggested Nao-chan could be protecting Kaori from SeKaori, since Sekai never takes control when Nao is present. Maybe Kaori wished for a way to deal with SeKaori.

I have a long and crazy ramble for the ones that like that sort of thing:
Hmmm, I think there's a good chance that the only reason as to why the cycles keep going is because Akira doesn't let them stop. I have a sort of theory on the back of my mind that whenever Akira is factory-reset he's brought back to the room with the clocks, and the original Akira can choose to put another clock on the wall/continue the cycle, or finally admit defeat and accept the end of the world. In this theory, original Akira is searching for something - which may very well be a way to bring Sekai back, or bring Maya back, or cure his psychosis, I have no idea (there are evidences to all of them) - but he keeps pressing the button until he finds the one "universe" where things will change, and by things, that could possibly just mean him.

All this children of the clockwork may just be the cogs in the system that he put up, by himself or with the help of someone else (perhaps even supernatural). The gods are part of the system, this much NAO has pointed at, as she herself is (and above them). Maybe they treat our Akira as an inferior thing because he is one, he's not the whole Akira, he's a fragment. Another in a cycle of thousands of fragments that they have watched try everything and fail, only for the actual Akira to hit the button and try again. Well, without going too deep in this theory, if this is correct in some form, then the answer is simple: to kill the gods and the system simply means to restore himself. Remember everything, learn how to deal with his trauma, get to the room with the clocks, and accept the end. System powers off, show's done.

Another possibility is taking control of the system, which may be what he's looking for if his intent is to bring Sekai back or something like that. Cause Sekai's dead, his only shot of bringing her back is inside whatever the cycles are. Sekai herself tells him this: if this world is made for him, then why wouldn't he be able to bring "her" back? (but actually just his vision/memory of her). HOPE can make anything a reality by editing the world, Wires can take control of everyone and make a city of puppets, Pareidolia seems to specialize in riding his mind. They're all the same thing, just different parts of it - editing reality, editing people, editing the user (Akira).

Even if what I said isn't the actual truth, I think it's unlikely that it isn't part of it. The religious symbolism and these gods, they're way too linked to Akira's childhood to not be a part of him, or created to suit him. And even if none of them are like this, and that it's just Akira perceiving NAO as Ami, or these gods as a manner to cope (HOPE = masturbate/sex), a dream to be in a safe place (Wires = replace the world with robots), or to embrace everything wrong within him (Pareidolia = enabling his inner voice to act out) - it's not like I have another protagonist to follow in order to get a clear picture lol

Another important thing to take notice of is that these three (actually four) are the same being. They're separated now yes, but even when Wires' story is first introduced, narrator says that it's an alternate version of Nozomu's creation story, for people that would rather have a scientific explanation. So, the thing is, it's not 4 different entities, it's one entity, that is acting as four at the moment. Well, who the hell would be Nozomu HOPE, Wires, Pareidolia and USER4 put together? In the form of a cross, stinking with symbolism that Saki pushed onto Akira, and that resembles the "T" from Teacher Sekai, and also a teacher that Akira became?

Remember that all users take turns controlling his terminal. It would make a lot of sense for USER4 to be Sekai, and for all gods together to simply be himself. But hey, it's just a crazy theory. Take from it whichever parts you may find more plausible. Also do not forget about that freaking tree that Tsubasa has at her house, cause that is a whole thing that I didn't cover in my mad ramble.

And I have a short and practical answer, for people that aren't insane:
//////////////////////YOUR QUERY IS FAULTY
/////////////////////THE ONE WITH WIRES CANNOT BE KILLED
////////////////////HIS SAMURAI HAS MASTERED THE DEADLIEST WEAPON

So, decided to go through the images and for those that like lore and not really understanding whether something means something or just looks cool, I noticed that there may be at least 2 more moons than those 3 Nodoka talked about and that false moon that Makoto mentioned (maybe).

Noriko seems to have a Pink Moon (Dark/Hot Pink?):
Sensei Narrator - "She is."
Noriko - "Sensei, I love you."
As implied by the pink light that tends to be around her, especially at night, but actually shown in the 'She Is' Chapter 3 Main Event, during Noriko's date dorm war with Futaba. (2nd Dorm Wars)

Then there's how Ayane apparently seems to have a Dark Moon:
Ayane - "Nevermind."
- "I love you..."
- "He changes all the time."
As shown during her 'Nevermind' Chapter 2 Event, which took place around the 3rd Reset (slumber party with Molly and Tsuneyo), and happens to be the one that mentions the Word of The Day; Perception, and tries to tell us about the Third god, before USER2 talks to us. Ayane was also briefly surrounded by green and blue light:
Ayane - "Maybe one day, far off in the future, you can teach me how to be as intentionally dense as you."
Before the green light seemed replaced by a Dark Moon. It happens to be the time she somehow got to the roof without a key at night, and is the reset she made it to the roof, only to vanish and lose the baby.

Later on in Chapter 2's 'Alderaan' Main Event, this Moon seems to show up again, with Blue light nearby. (2nd Beach Trip, and after Molly gets jealous over Otoha with Rin)

I have tried to take a look at the moons a couple of times and I think Selebus is just pulling this out of his ass. For green, blue and red I think there's enough of evidence in text for it to make sense (not necessarily moons, but colors themselves). Kaori is green and fears green. When Sekai is restored, there's a red and green color-grading on the doors. Nao-chan has red and green colored eyes. Red is considered bad by some. Narrator says someone in blue is there to help. Three gods, three colors. It's easier to accept that this was planned.

But if we try to find moons early on, or even go beyond these basic colors, we get a lot of stuff that makes it seem made-up.

For instance:
Is there a moon there? Is this red or pink? Does it even matter or is it just an effect to make the picture more into Noriko's colors since it's her leading the conversation?



How about this one? same issue: is this red? Is this pink? Is there a moon? Does it matter?


Is this green and pink? Green and red?


Well this certainly has a moon and is red - so should we just consider it when it's as visible and certain as this (with Sekai around the corner as well) or no?

Because then the moon isn't even red anymore...


And for as early as you get, the more confusing it gets also.

In my opinion, there is more to suggest that the moons and colors thing is a retcon than that they aren't. If we are to consider the moons to have meaning (I wouldn't go before the time Nodoka stated that they were important looking for clues), and just consider colors instead - since they have been mentioned enough that there is substance there since chapter 1 (or consider more the appearance of a moon, than their actual color).

As for colors, I wouldn't go beyond 3 colors, up to a maximum of 4 (as they appear in pictures - obviously there are more colors that matter, I just mean the ones that color the whole thing). Those being red, green and blue, with the added "clear/white". So, for my own sanity, I'd probably consider either pink to be red, or pink being just a color to set the tone of the scene (that also counts for any color outside of the 4).

That being said, the points you have made make sense for the individual events they are applied to and I will of course read with interest any other developments regarding either colors or the moons, I just probably won't be doing that research myself until I can be proven wrong (which I hope I am) on the regard of Selebus just giving meaning to what previously could have been: "Ayane is hopeless, thus black moon" or "We're talking about a big moment for Noriko, put a big freaking moon there and make it pink because her hair is the same color. Now, look, guys, even the world is agreeing with her."

I have tried summing them up a few times in the past:
DeSkel15 said:
The first god is mentioned in the 'Rewrite' main event back in Chapter 1, the Narrator called it Nozomu, and a horny ball of light. Nozomu translates to "To Hope" or "Hope" in Japanese. HOPE just so happens to help Sensei to the roof during this Reset. It is also Summer at this point.

The second god is mentioned in 'There is Nothing' at the end of Chapter 1. The Narrator called it Calm (while the first is Callous), tree like and computer like, with wires, etc. Sensei also has to connect to USER2 who helps him get to the roof during this Reset. The third god is mentioned but only that it was Concerned. It is turning Winter around this time.

It's also revealed that there are 4 USERs. USER1 to USER4, which you can try connecting to. Only USER2 connects though.

By this point 'The Room With Clocks' Happy Event had occured, and in it, USER2 shows up:
View attachment 3059843
and with this, that purple smily face, computer, Ramen bowl, and bird (probably Noodles), are inferred to be related to USER2, and by context, it also seems to be The Second god aka The Wire god (this name shows up later).

By the 'Word of The Day' Main Event in Chapter 2, not only do we have Tsuneyo showing up with this shirt from her father:
View attachment 3059846
But we also have USER2 showing up talking to Sensei with this "face":
View attachment 3059848 View attachment 3059860
We also have what appears to be USER2 showing up and talking about remaining Calm in it's unique way it communicates:
View attachment 3059859
So, yeah, it's heavily implied Tsuneyo is related to USER2 who seems at least related to the Wire/Calm god.

In the Trinity Happy Events there are loads of god lore. Most notably in the Trinity p2 one, a voice says Kill the Callous, Kill the Calm, Kill the Concerned. In Trinity p3, we have USER1 messing with Sensei, USER2 trying to connect, and USER3 then shows up:
View attachment 3059863 View attachment 3059864
With a male voice, talking in lower case, and noting it was "very concerned".

Later on in Sana's 'Ad Infinitum', this same USER3 seems to appear and name itself Pareidolia:
View attachment 3059867

By the end of Chapter 2, Sensei ends up back in HOPE's world in 'The Light of Last Summer', and notably refers to callousness:
View attachment 3059869

Then depending whether you chose Callous, Calm, or Concerned in a survey earlier, the 'Life of Prizes' Event will show you different books, which will talk to Sensei differently in this order:
View attachment 3059873 View attachment 3059875 View attachment 3059876 View attachment 3059877

Btw, I should mention that HOPE refers to itself as "The thing with Feathers":
View attachment 3059879
Most notably in the Trinity p3 Happy Event.

Anyway, just to sum it up, since there are dozens of events by this point in the game intended to give you an idea of the gods, one can Infer:
  1. First god is Callous, likely HOPE and The Lust Eater, and related to Yasu as even her church is known as the New Hope Church. Extra stuff that seems related: Birds, Light, TALKING IN CAPS, USER1, Summer, The Bottom of Everything, Angels, etc. Probably related to Ami.
  2. Second god is Calm, likely The Wire god, and related to Tsuneyo as her shirt, "son" Noodles, and Ramen itself seems related to this god, who seems heavily implied to be USER2. Extra stuff that seems related: Being in Darkness (confusingly), The Old District, visual changes, slanted all caps like this: "////CALM", Winter, Affection points, etc. Also Resets, and this is the one that made Maya think she'd be Reset during the 'Scary Room'. Probably related to Maya.
  3. Third god is Concerned, virtually guaranteed to be Pareidolia, USER3, and "The Dark". Extra Stuff that seems related: Spiders, Perception, Spring, talking in lower case, Kaori (Mistress of The Dark, and Queen of Spiders), etc. It also seems likely that The Shapeshifter and Ayane are related to this god. Maybe Sana and Yumi as well.
Beyond these 3 gods there also seems to be The Old One:
View attachment 3059904 View attachment 3059903
Nao:
View attachment 3059905
And The World Itself:
View attachment 3059957 View attachment 3059907 View attachment 3059955
The World Itself seemingly being the most malicious of the bunch:
View attachment 3059909 View attachment 3059910
It's likely related to Nodoka:
View attachment 3059911
And the Scary Sekai. Also seemed to be what fucked with Makoto:
View attachment 3059912
Btw, I should mention that like how Nozomu can translate to "Hope". Sekai can translate to "World". USER3/Pareidolia even seems to refer to Sekai as The World:
View attachment 3059916 View attachment 3059917 View attachment 3059918 This is Pareidolia comparing Sensei and Yumi to Sekai and Sensei for obvious reasons:
View attachment 3059921 View attachment 3059922

It isn't clear who or what USER4:
View attachment 3059951
is yet, as far as I can tell.

Overall: This is a summarization. If you want specifics, I'll try to show what I can. There's still a lot of unknowns though.

DeSkel15 said:
I've talked about the gods a few times before, if you want to use the search bar, you can probably find my past posts.

Anyway, the gods and users seem connected:
  • USER1 seems to be the First god mentioned, aka The Callous, The Lust Eater, Nozomu, and likely HOPE. Tends to talk in all caps "LIKE THIS". It's season is Summer.
  • USER2 is likely the Second god mentioned, aka The Calm, and The Wire god. Tends to talk in all caps with slants "/////LIKE THIS". It's season is Winter.
  • USER3 is the Third god mentioned, aka The Concerned, The Dark, and later on calls itself Pareidolia. Tends to talk in lower case, but can change it up whenever apparently. This is likely the one you saw talking in lower case. It's season is Spring.
Terminal 23 seems to be this World, but it isn't exactly clear yet. USERS and gods are somewhat interchangeable.

Why the First god aka The Callous shares a name with Sensei's brother isn't clear, but it's possible that it is simply the name the Narrator chose to give it. Nozomu can translate to Hope. Not to mention, who the Narrator telling us about the gods, is, also isn't clear. Also, probably should mention that USER1 has apparently account shared before, which makes things even more confusing.

As for what USER2/The Second god seems to want? Well, presumably it wants order:
View attachment 3250915 Narrator - "Because somewhere in this god's code, there was a line or two stating that he must maintain order."
Out of all of the gods and USERS, this one seems be the one behind the resets, memory alteration, and perception alteration that's likely going on. It's been noted that this god can:
View attachment 3250918 Narrator - "Sometimes, if he's controlling the right person, he can make some visual alterations as well."
At least alter visuals, and certain events like 'The Scary Room' Main Event, show that Maya at least thinks it could reset her. Not to mention, stuff like affection points seem to be it's thing. The game parts of this game seems to be it's domain.

Overall: It's not impossible that The Second god may be the system itself, or at least has control over it.

The First god seems to want this power, hence HOPE being implied to want something to do with wires and Sensei's special ability. Ironically, this Callous god may be the only one that's actually on Sensei's side, at least in theory, whether that's a "good" thing is up to you.

The Third god on the other hand seems to just want to make things how it thinks things should be.

Also some notable spoilers are that all 3 of these gods apparently gave Sensei his body, can't feel on their own, and require sacrifices that more or less translate to Sensei taking things that don't belong to him. They seem to need Sensei to fuck specific girls to maintain their power.

View attachment 3272585 Sensei - "Who...are you?..."

The interesting thing about HOPE (Assuming it's Yasu's god), is that it actually seems childish and young (for a god):
Yasu - "He's feeling shy tonight and doesn't want to talk to me."
- "But that's okay. He is all powerful, but can act a little childish at times."
- "He's still very young, all things considered."
(Yasu's Chapter 2 'Armor of Older Gods' Event)

Yet wants to fix Sensei and everything:
Yasu/HOPE(?) - "I CAN FIX YOU"
Yasu - "I can fix you."
- "I can fix everything."
(Chapter 2 Main Event 'Lavender's Blue')
It also seems to heal Sensei when he's hurt, and makes him feel safe:
Sensei Narrator - "The strange creature grows invisible arms (I think, I can't really tell.) and reaches toward me."
- "It heals my wounds in an act of mercy."
- "It is cold to the touch, but somehow makes me feel safe."
(Happy Event Trinity p2 'Hell is Empty')

Whether or not any of the gods are actually villains or are simply trying to appease a villain (or simply survive), is something I’ve been wondering more and more.

Seeing as how HOPE apparently can't exist outside Kumon-Mi:
Yasu - "There is no reason to leave this city, for He can not exist outside of its area of effect. And without Him, I am even closer to nothing than I was the day I was born."
I wonder if whatever is outside Kumon-Mi may be the real threat in this game.

Whether or not any of the gods are actually villains or are simply trying to appease a villain (or simply survive), is something I’ve been wondering more and more.
[...]
Seeing as how HOPE apparently can't exist outside Kumon-Mi:
I wonder if whatever is outside Kumon-Mi may be the real threat in this game.
Click to expand...
I don't think they're villains (in the sense that they were just born evil). But more that we're seeing the end of maybe thousands of years of these entities having to learn from fragments of Akira inside of cycles. In "tick tock tick tock", Am I Okay straight up says that she can get pregnant from Akira, with a new HOPE, and they can teach it to reset the world and touch him sexually.

Who even knows what Original Akira has done either to create, or affect these beings. All the horrible things they have ever said are either things Akira thinks about doing, or has done before. When NAO welcomes him to the Wishing Well, he cannot see himself - and she teases him about it - yet we know from the audio transcript that when he looks down into the well he's supposed to see himself. The logical answer would be that he is seeing himself - NAO is himself, all of this is himself, just not this fragment, but they're all fragments of the whole bigger Akira.

I think there's a high chance that the gods are either simply cogs that reacted to many cycles of Akira and are trying to do their job, or they're beings that gained sentience and are trying to keep the cycles going because they are a subproduct of it. In fact, Yasu says a couple of times that "He is the youngest of them, but dying all the same." - All these gods are dying. Why are they dying and how does Akira fit in their salvation is a question I'd like to have answered - because for all of HOPE's posturing, I don't see anyone else in this city being used by them in the way only Akira is (Not even going into Pareidolia, as he's literally inside of Akira's head ).

That also puts Himawari and the gods in check - Himawari needs the cycles to end in order to be born, the gods (and Sekai) need the cycles to keep going in order to be alive. SeKaori would be an alternative for Sekai to be alive if the cycles ended though. aramaug, this might be relevant to your Kaori theory.

Edit: also, I get why you're saying that Yasu's god hasn't been confirmed to be HOPE, but c'mon, we literally have to use HOPE as a key to understand what it says (apart from so many other evidences):
I say this less for myself, and more so that people can have at least some confirmation of something, it's already rare in this game lol

posts.content_html_raw: So i finished the summer vacation special event and i met Tree for the first time.Im currently going through Rins post rejection events and she gave me an idea for a theory.We know that Tree is either responsible for creating this world or is at the very least directly involved in it since the core characteristic of this world is for us(sensei) to be happy,and Tree feeds of hapiness.Now i will give this a more symbolic approach.We know that there is some sort of...invisible force compelling the girls(excluding Maya except that one handjob even where she was crying so she WAS concious but not able to control her body)to do stuff.For example when Sana said that she doesnt know why she is standing at the hallway,she just is.That force symbolically wise is Trees metaphorical roots digging deeper into the ground.The bigger Tree gets the stronger the illusion becomes.So when the thing thats antithetical of joy(misery) enters these girls hearts they temporeraly break off the illusion(Rin heard clocks ticking in the height of her misery).Anyways thats my rumblings for now.Im not proposing this theory as anything seriosu btw.This post and all the others that will follow until i finish the game are just me documenting my journey through the game and sharing it with you guys.So just enjoy the ride and dont think too much about it.Praise be!

Nadekai said:
... What is this upside-down house everyone mentions here ...
... What does is symbolize ...
Click to expand...
I'm not entirely sure.

It seems to be related to Futaba and Nodoka, as Futaba's Chapter 1 'Upside Down' Event more or less introduced this "Upside Down House" through a notebook that was apparently from someone in it:
Sensei - "You see, this house is upside down."
Albeit, it seemed to have multiple narrators. Meanwhile, Nodoka has seemingly drew this house in her Chapter 2 'I See Everything' Event:
Sensei Narrator - "Just childish drawings of what looks like a house."

Ami may have as well in Noriko's 'I Really Want to Stay at Your House' Chapter 3 Event:
Ami - "I've actually been wanting to show you this thing I drew the other day. It's..."
If you're not fucking her.

Presumably, it's also related to Sensei's and Nodoka's mothers, and possibly to Sel's last game 'Nothing is Beautiful'. Noriko has watched it, it's appeared during resets and happy events, it's appeared on TV with Otoha, and Niki. Etc.

Sensei even seemed to see it through static:
Sensei Narrator - "The TV is playing a show about several girls in a large house."
- "One of them is dead inside of a boiler room and the rest of the girls are either ignoring it or haven't found out yet."
In the 'There Is Nothing' Chapter 1 Main Event.

Overall: It's appeared and been mentioned numerous times, but why, isn't clear.

It may be the house that Possessed Tsuneyo recently mentioned:
Tsuneyo - "There are clues in a house near a lake. It started before you were born."
In her 'TH15 15NT M3' Chapter 4 Event.

If so, this Upside Down House may be where the supernatural stuff started, or at least could be related to the origin of things.

And each time she watched it, it was showing different things. However, she noticed that as she watched it in the dorms (outside of the old district), it changed to them eating some sort of grey substance (whereas it was real food when she watched it before).

From a different angle, there is a note somewhere about a woman that had to follow the rules of the house - and that makes me think that the upside down house might have been Sekai's childhood home (she didn't have a good relationship with her parents apparently, since she refused to answer when being called her family name).

That could mean that the upside down house could be "grandma's home", that Ami mentions - in case that the grandma is Sekai's mother, instead of Saki. In Chapter 4's 'Goodnight, Moon' Main Event.

Three gods, three sides of a cross - they all begin with C: Callous, Calm, Concerned.

We can add a lot more to this, but since this isn't a thesis but just a random thought - I'll stop here. I don't think this Ami is USER4, but some other Ami could be. Three sides of a cross make a T, from Teacher Sekai. And what is the fourth side of Teacher Sekai, what is the part that was only added later? her daughter. And this would both be an entity that is formed prior the resets, and also resonate with Akira's own care for Ami herself. Because, just as he can be Callous, Calm and Concerned, he can also care for her, as we've seen.

Is USER4 the Caring god then? Or, if you don't agree with any of this, how about the C thing? Will USER4 also have a C? And if so, what will it be if not Caretaker or Collector?
Click to expand...
I love the idea of The Caretaker pointing to a Caring God, and that Ami is somehow connected. The stuff about "on the way to twenty-four" is a great catch, I don't see what it could mean except TERMINAL 24, which means Ami either somehow knows about a coming "mega reset" or maybe even has the ability to cause it herself.

When I thought about (some version) of Ami being involved in USER4, I wondered if it could have something to do with the mysterious "return to form," and I found something that I'm kicking myself for not noticing earlier:

Ami uses the phrase "return to form" four times. In "All For You" the narrator uses the specific term "fourth form" to refer to the emergence of a new God, who with all of the four symbolism is presumably USER4.
(ignore the highlighting, I had this screenshot saved for my Kaori post)
So I think "the two of US return to form" refers to two people/entities combining to form USER4. Since it's a return to form, I would think that USER4 was once whole, but was split into halves. Ami refers to (probably) herself as half of a whole:
In the context here, the "whole" is her mom, which could have unsettling implications for the nature of a reformed USER4.

If one of the halves is (some version of) Ami, who is the other? The narrator of "Miserably Ever After" also uses the phrase, so I assume that narrator is either Ami or the other half of US. This might sound crazy, but I have a theory for who it is:
I think it's (some version of) Maya.

I haven't fully fleshed out the idea and will need to look back at a bunch of material, but here are some reasons why I think this.

Nao-chan is restored from a backup from USER4. Nao-chan has one of Ami's eyes and one of Maya's eyes.

There are A LOT of instances of the colors red (Ami/Sekai) and green (Maya) being juxtaposed in the game. This is something I'm going to have to pay more attention to on my second playthrough.

When Ami is talking about the "return to form" in "Not the Nightingale," there is a Maya silhouette on the wall, and she goes on to talk about "the shape of the proper silhouette." She also refers to "the girl [Sensei] used to love" who "vanished" - surely talking about Maya, I don't think she would describe Sekai as a "girl" (this has the additional implication that Ami knows Sensei loved Maya and that Maya Prime vanished).

The narrator of "Miserably Ever After" seems to also be the narrator of "Rhythm of a Black Heart". Both refer to Akira as a "former hero" and directly address the player as opposed to Akira. This narrator apparently wants to help Akira, but also talks about him being a terrible person. Sounds like positions Maya Prime would hold.

The narrator of "Miserably Ever After" says "I know from experience that wires can only do so much." There were indications that Wires was the God (or one of the Gods?) that Maya Prime followed, but she no longer wanted much to do with the Gods in the current timeline.

I don't think the voice that Ami talks to in "You & Me Against the World" is Sekai, Ami wouldn't say "Shut up" to the mom that she practically worships. One of the times the voice apparently interrupts her is when she's talking shit about Maya and saying Maya never cared about Sensei. Could Maya (Prime?) be talking to her?

The narrator starts talking about the "fourth form" in "All For You," an event about how one or more of Ami/Maya/Ayane are lying to each other and to Sensei. I think this narrator is Himawari, who would of course think Sensei can trust Ayane, and thus she indicates that both Ami and Maya are untrustworthy. I suspect current Ami and Maya Prime both know far more about the nature of the world and the resets than they have been letting on to Sensei.

Yasu : if this continues your soul is going to stray even farther from his light and then the darkness is going to devour it piece by piece.

Sensei : I had no idea that my soul is still there nor did i know that my soul really is MY soul to even begin with so i don't really mind it getting eaten.

Yasu : lost lamb you're looking for someone to save you, to rescue you.

Sensei : Well not right now but maybe when the next reset comes i may need some help.

Yasu : it is HE who can help you. but you're too far away from his light. so he told me to help you. to guide you back to his warmth. for HE is the one that saves us all from our terrible fate.

Sensei : and how are you going to "guide" me? i told you that i'm not a religious person so i won't -

-Suddenly Yasu reaches for Sensei's hand and puts it on her left cheek.

Sensei :... uhhh.. your face is surprisingly cold despite blushing like that.

Yasu : I am aware that i am too undeserving to be ordered by him but his words are absolute for when HE speaks i listen and obey.

-Yasu then gets on her knees facing Sensei's crotch.

Sensei : ok hold on Yasu. if Touka found out about this she's really going to assassinate me herself.

Yasu : do not be afraid little lamb for this is for your sake and yours only.

Sensei :... whatever. just tell touka i didn't make you do this.

-Then Yasu unzips Sensei's zipper to meet his shaft.

-BUT THEN SUDDENLY THE CHURCH'S DOORS SLAM OPEN FROM THE INSIDE WITH HITMEN IN BLACK SUITS WITH PISTOLS ON THEIR HANDS POINTED AT SENSEI AND A DAMN CHOPPER APPEARED ABOVE THEM. then SOMEONE dramatically slides down that chopper using a rope. in tight clothes and ridiculously huge boobas she stands menacingly (yes that's her).

Touka :I told you i'm not going to let anyone hurt Yasu anymore Sensei. and i really meant that.

-Touka then approaches Sensei bare handed with a killing intent.

Sensei : Would you believe me if i said that i didn't ask h-

-Then Touka delivers a left leg to Sensei's head and he falls down unconscious.

after that Sensei wakes up in a white space ( cliche i know) and suddenly HOPE appears. but that's all i remember from that dream/nightmare.

the next day i woke up and decided to decrease the amount of time i spend on playing visual novels.

I've realized that I may have accidentally wrote a terrible fan-fiction here but eh~ it's not like LIL is a wholesome SFW game anyway.

Yasu told the emissary of Pegasus that she has laid the foundation for a New Hope populated by sunflowers, again connecting to Sekai. It seems to me like Sekai/Pareidolia are trying to corrupt Yasu's church and use it for their own purposes.

And who do we have visiting the church:
  • Sensei: has Sekai/Pareidolia inside of him
  • Kaori: has Sekai/Pareidolia inside of her
  • Sana: Pareidolia has been fucking with her mind and probably isn't done, given her rapid personality shift in Chapter 4
  • Nodoka: has apparently been receiving instruction/information from The World/Sekai
That leaves Touka as the odd one out. The Emissary of Pegasus did demand a sacrifice...
Click to expand...
Touka actually seems likely related to The World Itself/Sekai.

Sensei seemingly saw Sekai in Touka's place recently:
There's apparently a "ghost" that wants her baby at the Tsukioka manor:
Tsukasa - "Some say she's still buried beneath it. And that the only reason she's haunting us is because her baby wasn't buried with her..."
And Yasu seemed to suggest that the Tsukioka manor shouldn't exist (or was at least related to something that shouldn't), like she seems to do with Sekai later:
Yasu - "The way this steel box moves is wrong. It's as if it's going backwards...inching closer and closer to what should not belong. To what should not exist."
- "This world is a wonderful one, but there are things trying to exist here that simply shouldn't."
(It happens to be that Yasu mentioned an Interference and the ocean after implying the Tsukioka manor shouldn't exist in Chapter 3's 'Somewhere Far From Here', and Sekai later gets restored at the beach, by the ocean, and seemingly around a restaurant Touka had brought to the beach prior.)

There's also how it seems more or less confirmed that the everblooming tree in the Tsukioka manor is likely related to Sekai and maybe Nao:
With Sensei implying the tree was related to a former lover of his:
Tsukasa - "You said Mother showed you this room once before?"
- "Do you like it here? Is that why you wanted to come back?"
Sensei Narrator - "Today is unlike all the other days. Today I am free to do as I please under the shadow of a former lover."
- "To make her jealous sounds even sweeter than muddied honeycomb."
Then after this, and the mentioning of a ghost, a Narrator called him "Aki-kun":
Narrator/Sekai(?) - "Come, Aki-kun."
- "Take it."
In Tsukasa's 'Blood and Sunset' Chapter 4 Event. (Btw the Emissary of Pegasus showed up with Masks(?) from Sekai's 'Something Everyone Knows And Ignores' Happy Event:
And it happens to ask about the sunset which may be a Sekai thing. In other words; it may be related to her, and Yasu may be getting manipulated in many ways.)

Overall: I'd be a little surprised if the Tsukiokas aren't linked to Sekai/The World Itself.
Taking into account how Kaori (who seems related to the Concerned god), seems possessed by a Sekai, how SeKaori seems to be trying something with Tsuneyo (who seems related to the Calm god), and how Touka has more or less adopted Yasu (who seems related to the Callous god), things seem to be going in Sekai's favor.

Possibly even more so than can be understood considering she may be the reason the other school collapsed. This got Sensei involved with the Tsukiokas, and the Nakayamas, and got the likes of Nodoka and Otoha close to him. I'm also somewhat thinking she wanted Ami to have Niki and Noriko to rely on beyond Sensei, when everything goes to shit, but who knows.

on the way to twenty four? what twenty four, Ami? TERMINAL 24? And every day you grow some more is the name of the very first event:
View attachment 3719245
Click to expand...
I've been thinking some more about Ami's apparent mention of TERMINAL 24, and how the other things she says in the same event could be clues regarding what a TERMINAL is.
Everything Ami says has a reasonable surface-level interpretation, but if we assume that she's looking forward to TERMINAL 24, they take on different meanings (if "twenty-four = TERMINAL 24" is wrong, this post will sound very silly). I also assume that the reference to "Every Day I Grow Some More" means that the start of TERMINAL 24 will involve a full reset of Sensei and maybe even the start of a new "game".

Ami wants to "fix" Sensei, but in typical Ami fashion that actually means she wants to keep him broken so that they can live in unhealthy co-dependency with no one else involved.
So she talks about taking him to somewhere that no one can find him

So far this has a reasonable interpretation that Ami wants to move again and ghost everyone like they did when they left the Old District. But she also says she wants to go somewhere that isn't in Kumon-mi
which on the surface doesn't make much sense when it's supposedly impossible to physically leave Kumon-mi.

Everything takes on a different meaning if we assume she's talking about moving to TERMINAL 24. That would mean that TERMINAL 24 is an entirely new location, not just a fully reset Kumon-mi/TERMINAL 23. So maybe each TERMINAL is a different version of Kumon-mi. Or maybe they're actually completely different locations, with Sensei's memories altered to match the new TERMINAL.

If she's talking about moving to TERMINAL 24, that means she thinks that no one else will be able to find them there. As for why she thinks that, there is a very telling line when she is supposedly talking about keeping Uta and Io out of the house:
It makes little sense for her to refer to Uta and Io as "bugs". Instead it sounds like she's talking about computer bugs, further suggested because we see Ami's laptop in the background.

As for what program the bugs are part of, here's an idea: Kumon-mi itself is controlled by a computer program, and TERMINAL 23 is the "developer interface" to that program. I don't mean that the people in it are part of the program (or at least not the named characters, the faceless people might be for all that they matter), but rather how the city itself seems to evolve or change over time, which sometimes has dramatic effects on the story. One example would be the sinkhole, which brought more girls into Sensei's life and so would be viewed as a bug by Ami.

One last thought on bugs: the fact that Ami thinks she could have kept them out indicates she has (or had) some degree of control over TERMINAL 23, which is more support for her being connected to USER4.
That analysis might feel pretty tenuous. So of course I'm now going to double down and use even flimsier evidence to speculate further.
I wonder if the Great Pareidolia Mall (GPM) is the remnants of an old TERMINAL.

First there's the idea that Akira helped pull "number 17" from Amy's mouth the last time she saw him.
"Number 17" is a very particular and odd phrase to use to refer to a tooth, and Amy never explicitly says that it is a tooth she's talking about. Instead, maybe it's referring to the creation of TERMINAL 17, either because Ami/Amy has something to do with the creation of the TERMINALs, or because "number 17" refers to "Ami/Amy #17" who is created to inhabit TERMINAL 17. (Either way, that would mean GPM is TERMINAL 16.)

Amy says she's only met Akira once before, but she's too familiar with him for that to be true



The last one implies they used to date, and at another point she tells him "I love you", so it's reasonable to assume that there used to be a version of Akira living in GPM and that he was the ex-boyfriend that Ami definitely didn't throw through the hole in the mall
Falling for eternity evokes the constant imagery of Sensei falling and in particular how the game began with Sensei literally falling (and entering TERMINAL 23?). So when ex-boyfriend Akira helped pull "number 17" from her mouth and was definitely not thrown through the hole, he could have been sent to the next TERMINAL.

There's also a direct suggestion that GPM is similar to Kumon-mi in how they both grow and evolve over time
and like Kumon-mi, it has a world "outside the walls"
But it might have been around for much, much longer


(The idea being that GPM started at the size of Kumon-mi or even just the Kumon-mi Mall, but has continued to expand over time.)
There's also the general dilapidated condition of the mall and the fact that Amy talks about other residents, but we obviously never see them, and she might actually be the only one left

If GPM is a former TERMINAL, there are two passages of Amy's dialogue that I find especially interesting. First, describing the mall as alive:
A "living thing" that continues to iterate on itself could be a computer program. If the part about GPM sucking in people also applies to other TERMINALs, it could explain why the girls that Ami wants to avoid keep showing up even though they aren't supposed to (and by "fixing the bugs" she wants to prevent it in the future).

The second interesting passage is regarding Amy's memories:

Amy lost most of her memories before she came to the mall but crucially she still retains some things. These might be memories from the Ami/Amy in the previous TERMINAL. Or they might be memories from an Ur-Ami who is outside of the TERMINALs and is likely part of USER4. In either case, it would help explain why current Ami knows more than she should.

Moonflare said:
oooooh, I smell a new game in our hands! What is something that annoys you in not having been resolved yet? It doesn't have to be the most annoying thing in terms of the whole story, it could be something small, but what just annoys you personally?

Like you think to yourself "for how long are we gonna have to wait yet?" or "Man, this situation is just getting ridiculous..."

For me, it's the Chika thing - I thought it was bizarre from the first scene when she overreacted by Akira mentioning Niki, and it's been seasons of everyone accepting that he dated her, and yet here we are years later.

For me it's the Nodoka book thing. As soon as it was introduced, I felt there was no way it couldn't have immediate and probably massive "real world" impact. Then nothing happened. Then Futaba found out, and I thought certainly NOW something has to happen. Then nothing happened. There are so many people whose lives stand on a knife's edge if just one wrong person finds out - like, what happens to Sensei if noted reader Wakana spots the book in a store, recognizes the author's surname, and flips through it? And yet no one seems to care except Futaba, and she hasn't done much more than make a frowny face. Hopefully it finally goes somewhere in this update with the Futaba events, but I'm not optimistic.

In contrast, I don't mind the Chika thing nearly as much as everyone else. To me, it makes a lot more sense than Nodoka's book from a character perspective; Chika keeps getting hints, but she never follows them up and finds out because she's scared of finding out. Though I imagine my patience is also helped by the fact that I haven't been sitting around waiting for updates in "real time" yet.

Still, Sel definitely seemed aware that Yumi needed others to be interesting, hence Futaba, Nodoka, Sensei, etc, all kind of being forced to be involved with her as if Kumon-Mi literally forced them together:
View attachment 3725665 Yumi - "It's like the fucking city itself keeps trying to force us together and not realizing that I hate your fucking guts."
(Albeit, in theory it/The World Itself literally was forcing Yumi and Sensei together).

Now, that role seems to be falling to Noriko and Io to spice things up. (Chika has always been there, but she's becoming redundant as I'm sure others are starting to see. Her and Uta almost fighting over Io and Yumi is interesting though.)

I'm not even sure if Yumi will be remembered by anyone after Sensei fucks her, as whether "she got the dick yet" seems to be her main selling point to fans. I wouldn't be surprised if some are only playing to finally get to that point, then will lose interest. Might even be why it hasn't happened.

Interestingly, Yumi is one of my favorite characters, and for reasons that have very little to do with how much I want to see her get a good dicking. I can agree that her backstory and the delinquent tsundere persona aren't very interesting, but I think she has actual depth of character beyond that. For one thing, she might be the only member of the main cast that has any sort of inner conflict over her feelings towards Sensei that lasts longer than two seconds. Yeah, she obviously has a crush on him, but it feels like she really wished she didn't a lot of the time. She can get seriously skeeved out by him and feels a lot of guilt due to her loyalty to Chika (and knowing that he's "cheating" on her), even without acting on her feelings. She tries to grapple with what she knows about his dark side, whereas every character that knows more than her either has unconditional love toward him or is sociopath with an extremely punchable face (not to name names).

I also enjoy the effect she has on Sensei. Because he knows about the complexity of her feelings (and her connection to his blackouts) he tends to get more introspective around her and even sometimes allows himself to be vulnerable.

I started trying to order the main characters by how cliche I find them and it took me a while to get to Yumi. For me, Molly, Miku, Ayane, Touka, and Rin are all definitely more cliche (I forgive Rin and Molly because they're funny). Otoha is only not more cliche because she is somehow still a complete non-character. Sana would have been on the list until recent developments. And while they're not cliche per se, Uta and Noriko still feel more one-dimensional.

"Number 17" is a very particular and odd phrase to use to refer to a tooth, and Amy never explicitly says that it is a tooth she's talking about. Instead, maybe it's referring to the creation of TERMINAL 17, either because Ami/Amy has something to do with the creation of the TERMINALs, or because "number 17" refers to "Ami/Amy #17" who is created to inhabit TERMINAL 17. (Either way, that would mean GPM is TERMINAL 16.)

Falling for eternity evokes the constant imagery of Sensei falling and in particular how the game began with Sensei literally falling (and entering TERMINAL 23?). So when ex-boyfriend Akira helped pull "number 17" from her mouth and was definitely not thrown through the hole, he could have been sent to the next TERMINAL.

Amy lost most of her memories before she came to the mall but crucially she still retains some things. These might be memories from the Ami/Amy in the previous TERMINAL. I quite like these ideas. However, there are some things that we should establish. TERMINAL 23 has been reset many times during the gameplay, but what about factory resets? There is evidence that the factory reset happens in the room with the clocks, mainly because that's what the Scary Room turns into as Maya is about to be factory reset. My point is: Has Maya Prime always been in TERMINAL 23? Cause if so, the changing of Terminals isn't related to Akira being factory reset.

And if every time he's factory reset is linked to a change in terminals, then 23 seems way too little. So either terminals have nothing to do with cycles, or each terminal can hold hundreds of cycles of factory resets. Like the entirety of Maya's Prime journey would be inside of TERMINAL 23. Back to the room with the clocks, we're shown the room that predates the current cycle, in which Moyo and YouDidIt are around an Akira that behaves as a puppet to a different God that wants to see him dance (which is what NAO commands him to do). aramaug said:
Interestingly, Yumi is one of my favorite characters, and for reasons that have very little to do with how much I want to see her get a good dicking. I can agree that her backstory and the delinquent tsundere persona aren't very interesting, but I think she has actual depth of character beyond that. For one thing, she might be the only member of the main cast that has any sort of inner conflict over her feelings towards Sensei that lasts longer than two seconds. Yeah, she obviously has a crush on him, but it feels like she really wished she didn't a lot of the time. She can get seriously skeeved out by him and feels a lot of guilt due to her loyalty to Chika (and knowing that he's "cheating" on her), even without acting on her feelings. She tries to grapple with what she knows about his dark side, whereas every character that knows more than her either has unconditional love toward him or is sociopath with an extremely punchable face (not to name names).

I also enjoy the effect she has on Sensei. Because he knows about the complexity of her feelings (and her connection to his blackouts) he tends to get more introspective and even sometimes allows himself to be vulnerable around her.

I started trying to order the main characters by how cliche I find them and it took me a while to get to Yumi. For me, Molly, Miku, Ayane, Touka, and Rin are all definitely more cliche (I forgive Rin and Molly because they're funny). Otoha is only not more cliche because she is somehow still a complete non-character. Sana would have been on the list until recent developments. And while they're not cliche per se, Uta and Noriko still feel more one-dimensional.
Click to expand...
I feel like most of the other girls with conflicts about liking Sensei, have more interesting reasons why. Uta has Io and her past, Tsuneyo sees him as a predator and possibly a rapist of her friend, Sana saw him as her best friend's love interest, doesn't seem actually interested in romance, and seems to have a rape fetish, not to mention absent father and a mother that crushes on him, Rin realizes he's old and she prefers girls, but also values him as a homie and has basically a sister, mother figure, and first crush, going after him, etc.

I struggle to see how any of those girls you mentioned, are more cliché than Yumi, tbh, but to each their own.

Because if he's fixed and starts acting like a normal human being, she's scared it will damage the connection between them. - "It's scary out there. That's why I keep you here."

It's likely why she wants to get pregnant so bad, why she likes the Nakayamas who are somewhat like sisters to her, and why Sara and Sana were invited in the 'Lamb Legs' Happy Event. Ami - "No one is drugging my uncle! You're all insane!"
Besides the recent break in, and wizard pic on his phone, Sensei also broke, and she had to take care of him for 2 months.

Interestingly, Yumi is one of my favorite characters, and for reasons that have very little to do with how much I want to see her get a good dicking. I can agree that her backstory and the delinquent tsundere persona aren't very interesting, but I think she has actual depth of character beyond that. For one thing, she might be the only member of the main cast that has any sort of inner conflict over her feelings towards Sensei that lasts longer than two seconds. Yeah, she obviously has a crush on him, but it feels like she really wished she didn't a lot of the time. She can get seriously skeeved out by him and feels a lot of guilt due to her loyalty to Chika (and knowing that he's "cheating" on her), even without acting on her feelings. She tries to grapple with what she knows about his dark side, whereas every character that knows more than her either has unconditional love toward him or is sociopath with an extremely punchable face (not to name names).
I also enjoy the effect she has on Sensei. Because he knows about the complexity of her feelings (and her connection to his blackouts) he tends to get more introspective and even sometimes allows himself to be vulnerable around her.
I started trying to order the main characters by how cliche I find them and it took me a while to get to Yumi. For me, Molly, Miku, Ayane, Touka, and Rin are all definitely more cliche (I forgive Rin and Molly because they're funny). Otoha is only not more cliche because she is somehow still a complete non-character. Sana would have been on the list until recent developments. And while they're not
cliche

I struggle to see how any of those girls you mentioned, are more cliché than Yumi, tbh, but to each their own.

I don't have a good explanation for the blindfolds yet, but I don't think it can just be a HOPE thing. I can't see any way that HOPE would be involved with the blindfolded "What's "A" Stand For?" rabbit, and I also find it pretty unlikely he's connected to the Abandoned Shrine. I would also be annoyed from a narrative perspective if the rabbit color is meaningless after it's been established that all of HOPE's (known) rabbits are black.
Click to expand...
A good thing to keep an eye on is that Yomiel wanted to change allegiances from HOPE to Wires (?) - gotta be Wires since Pareidolia wasn't a thing at that point. Also take note that the rabbits were designated to specific gods (maybe by NAO?).



If he managed to change between them, he would thus change colors if the theory holds true about colors being for each god. However he tried to run away from the Sekai restoration.

Also take notice that Yomiel denied being able to talk about Sekai (probably because he was ordered not to, since he knows about her as he knows she's coming), and this aligns with HOPE's proclamations that he was the one that brought her back (but this demands further investigation).



Later on we see Sekai returning with a rabbit, and logic would dictate that it was Yomiel being caught by her, but it was Penemue instead...


Now, if we ever see Penemue changing colors this would help in your theory since he was touched by Sekai. But on the same hand, she seems to return him to Yasu. So let's keep an eye on his appearance during her next events.
Other stuff related to Yasu, black, white, colors and the rope.
Now, one of the big confusions we have is about Pareidolia being "the dark" and Wires being "in darkness". Here's a part of Yasu's speech about it that we tend to overlook:

Pareidolia is the god of spring, and therefore he should not be associated with the things that exist inside of Winter and Summer. He's responsible for consuming spring, and thus what he brings with him when spring begins again, is something that was lacking in the world before that (he should be bringing the pinks and blues, and USER4 should be bringing the red and yellows).



So, for a while I was in doubt about if Pareidolia was the rope, but looking back after confirming the existence of USER4, that seems highly unlikely. Pareidolia is the god of spring, and therefore outside of the common tug of war between everything (HOPE) and nothing (Wires).



So, it can be misleading in the next bit because Yasu calls the rope a great divine, but one, Yasu doesn't know about Pareidolia, as she's confused in chapter 4 as to how spring is even a thing. What she's saying here is that Akira is the rope, and it's importance is similar to a divine entity. And also that if he snaps, they change the rope (factory reset him)



And then we have this:

This right here is Maya.


Notice the sole strand of hair over the eye. This is before Maya Prime gets factory reset, and to the right you can see the sakura blossom. Now, Sekai HATES Maya. So there shouldn't be a connection there, but what if the connection of shadow Maya is with, instead, the World Itself - maybe even being it.

There is a lot about her presence here since she could simply be in New HOPE church, she is haunting Akira, yet doesn't seem to ever interfere with him (she doesn't appear to him like Sekai does). My interpretation by her demeanor here is that she's in a position to speak in his ear, possibly being one of the narrators - yet he never heard or saw her before (which would also align with the narrators).

Why does she appear here though? Well, I think it's because she's the rope. Yasu says that the rope is something that lures those who grip it into believing the outcome is not predetermined. Now, who believes it is predetermined? NAO. Who doesn't? Some of the narrators, including Himawari. This entire cycle is about an unknown force (or multiple of them) making it different than a thousand other times.



Yasu says that the rope is one that wishes away the love of all the gods. The rope wants Akira to break free. Remember the room with the clocks? AmIOkay is trying to get Akira to escape, but he can't wake up from his blackout and instead she's stuck there.



Then, in tick tock tick tock, she keeps trying to teach Akira how to wake up and open the damn door



"the arms of the one person to have truly loved me". Yep, that's Maya. Which would also make the "i love you so much" hers too.



Additionally, the thing about a time when things were better should be about her as well, and a version of Ami being USER4 might hold some water based on Baby Finches as well (also take notice of the red and yellow).


Oh, and the one playing with spiders on the background is probably Kaori, same haircut and clothes. But I don't know what's at play here:



Also, the reason Maya avoids the old district might be because of Wires. She most likely prays to him to make the reset happen, and the green here might be evidence pointing out to green being his color (which we could investigate based on where green tones appear). That definition of what god is, that is definitely about Wires though:



So given all of that, I think that there is a Maya out there narrating things and being a fifth force in all of this (maybe along Himawari). NAO says that Akira is a thread hanging from a fraying rope, which could mean that the whole Akira is the actual rope - in which case, this shadow Maya might be together with him trying to get him to wake up before it's too late. Or it could mean that this "different" Akira is hanging from the efforts of the rope Shadow Maya.
Well, those are lots of new theories, and some more flimsy than others. I think there's a good chance Maya is the one saying "I love you so much" and that she's a narrator. Shadow Maya may be that very narrator, or she could be the World Itself (given the sakura trees). The rope choosing when it breaks could also mean that Maya broke Akira many times with her actions.

Anyway, it's a lot and I apologise for not properly weaving all of this into a unified theory, but I found some of them interesting and wanted to share right away.

Ayane - "I really like the name Ami, but that one's kind of already taken, so..."
- "I like A-Names if you couldn't tell. Like Ayane!"
- "Oh sorry, Your Ami, not our Ami. Our Ami hasn't been born yet."

Ayane - "I really love the summer, Sensei."
(Ayane's Chapter 3 'How the World Works' Event)

A hallucination(?) of Ayane also mentioned hearing Voices before:
Ayane(?) - "But I've been hearing things too, Sensei. Actual voices. That want me to do things for them that I don't want to do. And Ami heard...hears them too."
(Chapter 3's 'Meant to Be' Main Event)
And Makoto has described things she's heard as if the World was speaking to her:
Makoto - "It's like the world itself is speaking to me."
(Makoto's Chapter 3 'White Oak Door' Lust Event)
The fact that both these girls have more or less taken over the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad, have the color Blue as something seemingly notable about them, and had a death of something that mattered to them occur (Todd vs Makoto's dad), is all quite interesting.

Overall: Ayane may be influenced by Sekai/The World Itself. Both her and Sekai being mothers who "lost" their baby, and both being inherently eccentric, including in school, also seems suspect. It could even explain why Ayane seems so odd lorewise (at least to me).

Sensei Narrator - "Maya disappears, but I manage to find my way back home all by myself."
(Chapter 3's 'Times New Roman' Main Event)

Chinami - "Chinami doesn't like the silent method. She learns better when there are words involved."
(Chapter 4's Chinami 'Holden Caulfield' Event)

I have another thing that sat on my mind for some time now.

It's about bugs.
For long i wondered how bugs are connected to the story, and while what i came up with might not be the 100%, i guess it's close.

We have a couple of bug nets in some scenes, even one is a talking being with a knife for a mouth and whatever for eyes and speaking during some (reset/happy?) events.

So far what i got from animes and japanese games, bug hunting seems to be a thing in japan for kids.
Though i take this with a grain of salt, because those two sources might be overstatements.
Like cultural depiction in fiction vs real life.
Whatever.

Some people think that bugs are associated with Sekai.
And i share that opinion in this case.
I could see how Akira as a kid was into bug hunting, hence we get the bug hunting nets in some scenes (mostly reset/happy?).
They could be metaphors for a time Akira was into bug hunting and when he went out into the woods, he was accompanied by Sekai.
That might have been the first time and place he was "assaulted" by her.
Making it "their" special place (the woods/forrest), "a place where they can be free", "where nobody would find them".

Tl;dr
Bugs and bug hunting nets are metaphors for the time and place Akira and Sekai's "history" started.

derekthered56 said:
And I wonder if this plays into her being able to actually reject him, where the other girls would have begged forgiveness for having gotten upset.
Click to expand...
She didn't though. In Better Boy, Akira offers Karin a clean out and her exact words are:


Like, even taking this as hard as she could, she still only wants distance for a while. And during the conversation she's basicaly begging Akira to lie to her:



She wanted it to be real, and she wanted him to apologise and say that it was because he loved her. And she still wants for him to be able to love and possibly fall in love with her (my take).
So yeah, in terms of rejection, Yumi's the one that really rejected him. Granted, he actually went through with it with Yumi - he managed to stop with Karin, only tackling her down. Also, even Noriko "rejects" him harder than Karin in my opinion, cause even though she proclaims her love for him and that she'll get over it...


but she doesn't though, it takes a long ass time. Not even going into how Noriko doesn't apologise but tells him to change.

I do agree though that the Kanda sisters reasoning for being into Akira is kinda shallow. Kirin just wanted to be seen and used sex for that, then as Akira treats her like the trash she is, and points out that's not what she wants, she wants to be an actual person cause of course she does, she's a fucking bad joke.
And Karin I think ultimately wants to fall, from what I get, her life is stifling. So talking to a teacher more than necessary, to eventually going on dates, to picture a life as his wife, to sort of compete with her sister for his affection - those are all not Karin things to do, and yet are the very things that break from her need to be perfect. The issue is, she hasn't had to confront it until "Paranoid". All she ever did with him had the convenience of not having to be addressed because Akira simply didn't take that step (although she gave him every cause to do it). In real life, a female teenager student doesn't invite Akira to dine at her house in secret from her parents and gets to pretend that this is normal, and not at all flirting/a romantic date.

Think about it, if you take out Pareidolia forcing him to do it, would it be so strange if he tried to kiss Karin? They're in this back and forth for years now, where she bakes him cookies, takes him out on dates, invites him over to cook for him when her parents aren't at home - it's like she says, it would have been so easy for him to go like "well, I actually like you and I thought that from all things we did it was mutual". I really do think she wanted him to go "yes, I love you - and I'm sorry if I went about it the wrong way, but it doesn't change how I feel". The fact that she goes "keep away for a while" to me is a cop-out, when Akira is trying to get her to be free of him and deep down she doesn't want to.

Is she gonna deal with that or deny it super hard? I think that's the issue at hand. Because Akira tackled Wakana in a similar manner, and ok, Wakana is equipped as an adult to put him in his place, but did Karin really didn't want it to happen, or was just shocked by the manner in which it did? All in all, this is the most interesting thing to happen to her in her arc thus far (and probably what will make her deal with her sister finally progress).

I don't think Kirin will care that much either tbh, I think she's more afraid because she doesn't know what happened. As soon as she learns that "all that happened" was Akira tackling her and stopping it when she asked, and later apologising - I'd like a scene that Kirin just goes: "well, what the fuck did you expect a dude would do after you keep inviting him on dates and acting like you love him?" Or Kirin will actually flip and be a caring human being towards her sister, who knows...

Maybe the Kanda sisters will bond over their love for him, or start an actual rivalry - those would be interesting. I just don't see Kirin taking Karin's side (she's too dependent on Akira), but I might be wrong.

aramaug said:
There's an idea that I've been playing with, but I'm not sure yet if it stands up to any scrutiny. Is it possible that none of the Sekais we've seen (outside of memories/happy events) are real, and it's all just Pareidolia putting on a human mask?
Click to expand...
I don't think so, here's why: Pareidolia wants an infinite spring, yet there is an alternate power getting things ready for Fall. So something amid all of these Sekais has to be against Pareidolia. Allies in the sense of taking power back from Everything (HOPE) and Nothing (Wires), but ultimately adversaries in that for Fall to come, Spring has to end.

The rest is a ramble about how colors could help with that, feel free to skip if not interested in scraps of theories.
It could help us if we managed to determine which colors relate to which gods, or if the moons also relate to gods, and if so, again with which colors. I tried to bounce some ideas ahead, but feel free to skip as it doesn't go anywhere (may be useful for someone looking into colors though).

Event is "Frankincense": What Yasu says about colors (in my shadow Maya theory) may serve here, but this is weak overall and gets very convoluted in color gradings:


Black and White are from Winter and Summer. Red and Yellows are of the Fall, Pinks and Blues are of the Spring. This could mean nothing, but if it does - Sekai's restoration is both derived from Red (Fall) and Green (?).



Kaori's eyes are yellow and blue (Fall and Spring), her inside is Red (Fall). Also her self proclaimed color is green (which she also fears). And Yasu seems to fear only red (Fall). Nao-chan's eyes are green (?) and red (Fall). And Nao-chan's assigned color is purple, which is blue (Spring) + red (Fall).



I see two possibilities for the green enigma: either green simply means Wires, which is something many have pointed out as a possibility, or green means blue + yellow - in that case, green would mean Spring and Fall combined.

This got complicated, so here's the rundown:

Kaori is a being of Pareidolia + USER4 (but possibily put together by Wires). And when she turns into SeKaori she becomes a being of Fall.

Nao-chan is a being of USER4 + Wires (but brought forth by both Pareidolia and USER4).

Sekai is a being of USER4 + Wires (?).

Yeah, maybe I'm going about this wrong, but I'll leave it here in case parts of it are useful to someone
Basically, I think determining if green relates to Wires or not could turn out to be a huge deal, because it seemed to be related to Sekai's restoration. And I think green might be related to him, just as I think Wires might be Maya's god (and she's either lying about not knowing about him, or Maya Prime simply didn't remember this piece of information).

I have no idea. But Selebus being weird is not really a surprise. I will say though that I wouldn't go so far as to assume he's roleplaying a narrator in real life that can't talk about Himawari cause she's a bug.
And that's because YouDidIt (long maya) fully aknowledges Himawari during Untitled. Himawarico is super present nowadays too. So she talks to people other than Akira, is aknowledged by the children of the clockwork, is a narrator and has a successful enterprise lol

Also, the narrators sometimes reference one another, during the auto-pilot disengage sequence there is a narrator that receives a notice from the desk of the ninth god, chooses to disregard it, and straight up says Pareidolia will have their head for it. He probably just doesn't want to talk about her at all due to her being such a big thing and important to his story (simply confirming that she is Himawari, for instance, is already to confirm something that hasn't been confirmed in game).

Then again, who knows. My professional opinion is to disregard Selebus as much as possible outside of what he writes into the game. And since the wiki is fanmade, I think it's more likely to keep it spoiler-free/not knowing what to call her as her name hasn't been revealed, than anything else.

Edit: Also, Himawari is much less a bug than a freelancer. What's different about her is that she's a possibility, so it's not really a bug because her existence isn't even a reality yet. I think if we were to use the word bug, that would much more apply to Nao-chan/TEMPLATE 9, because she's something referenced many times as something that should not exist, which is what a bug is. If Akira gets Ayane pregnant, and she has the child and they name her, boom, Ami Arakawa the second Himawari is born, no bugs there.

Moonflare said:
I don't think so, here's why: Pareidolia wants an infinite spring, yet there is an alternate power getting things ready for Fall. So something amid all of these Sekais has to be against Pareidolia. Allies in the sense of taking power back from Everything (HOPE) and Nothing (Wires), but ultimately adversaries in that for Fall to come, Spring has to end.

The rest is a ramble about how colors could help with that, feel free to skip if not interested in scraps of theories.
It could help us if we managed to determine which colors relate to which gods, or if the moons also relate to gods, and if so, again with which colors. I tried to bounce some ideas ahead, but feel free to skip as it doesn't go anywhere (may be useful for someone looking into colors though).

Event is "Frankincense": What Yasu says about colors (in my shadow Maya theory) may serve here, but this is weak overall and gets very convoluted in color gradings:
View attachment 3731421

Black and White are from Winter and Summer. Red and Yellows are of the Fall, Pinks and Blues are of the Spring. This could mean nothing, but if it does - Sekai's restoration is both derived from Red (Fall) and Green (?).

View attachment 3731425

Kaori's eyes are yellow and blue (Fall and Spring), her inside is Red (Fall). Also her self proclaimed color is green (which she also fears). And Yasu seems to fear only red (Fall). Nao-chan's eyes are green (?) and red (Fall). And Nao-chan's assigned color is purple, which is blue (Spring) + red (Fall).

View attachment 3731442

I see two possibilities for the green enigma: either green simply means Wires, which is something many have pointed out as a possibility, or green means blue + yellow - in that case, green would mean Spring and Fall combined.

This got complicated, so here's the rundown:

Kaori is a being of Pareidolia + USER4 (but possibily put together by Wires). And when she turns into SeKaori she becomes a being of Fall.

Nao-chan is a being of USER4 + Wires (but brought forth by both Pareidolia and USER4).

Sekai is a being of USER4 + Wires (?).

Yeah, maybe I'm going about this wrong, but I'll leave it here in case parts of it are useful to someone
Basically, I think determining if green relates to Wires or not could turn out to be a huge deal, because it seemed to be related to Sekai's restoration. And I think green might be related to him, just as I think Wires might be Maya's god (and she's either lying about not knowing about him, or Maya Prime simply didn't remember this piece of information).
Click to expand...
Besides the narrator who rejected the infinite spring, is there evidence that someone else is trying to bring about fall?

I'd caution against reading too much into color choices in the Yasu quote. It would be nice if they meant something, but red is everywhere in the game's color symbolism while blue and pink are barely used and yellow not at all (I think). It could just be as simple as spring has blue and pink flowers and fall has red and yellow leaves. She seems to be trying to make a metaphor for why the return of spring is good, and that idea might not be coming from HOPE or at least was corrupted; this event is after SekaiDolia (I've decided it's a thing now) talked through her, and they would have much more reason to look forward to spring than HOPE would.

The colors (and colored moons) are still a mystery to me. It's something I'm trying to catalog on my second playthrough, hopefully that leads somewhere. I will say that red and green appear together so often that I think their combination has special meaning (and clearly that meaning is Ami + Maya = USER4, all the best people are saying it.).

And unrelated to this post, but since I don't think I've mentioned it before, I'll say that I'm all onboard with the idea that Himawari's real name is Ami. I named Ayane's baby Ami on my first playthrough because I assumed it was the "correct" answer.
