I think the big words for understanding Noriko are loser, genius and insane. I'll skip most of what has already been said in previous posts and instead focus on what I think hasn't been mentioned enough.

Also, this is a long only textual character analysis, if not interested, skip to the tacos at the end.
Noriko's been following Akira since she was born basically and been annoying to him all the while. He complains to Niki that she sticks to him like glue, and she agrees. This doesn't mean that Akira was averse to Noriko rather than just wanting to skip to spending time with Niki, but it does mean that Noriko's relationship with him was from the start her pestering him from attention and getting the scraps he was too pressured to not give her. This is the dynamic that worked for her = pester until he gives something back (which is the seed for stalker behavior).

She was never number one, and she knew she'd never be number one. So her idea of having her love reciprocated was skewed. Sexual awakening for her, which would be being intimate with someone else, was for her to hide in her sister's closet to see Akira being given oral. Not a one time thing either. She didn't wish for him to break up with her sister either, she again, just had to learn to accept whatever fell her way. Understanding this is vital to understanding how Noriko accepted/and still accepts being a loser in love.

Later, when she started being tutored, that was time she could have alone with him in a moment when Akira didn't spend as much time/and later time at all with her sister. That gave her hope she could be number one, especially cause there were other girls being tutored, and of those Noriko most likely was the special one to him. But then the stray arrived. Maya wasn't competing for anything from the start, she didn't have an hour of Akira's time a few days of the week, she lived with him. It was then that Noriko had to see a random girl that came out of nowhere become his number one after each passing week. A girl that was inherently hostile to her btw, different than what Niki was, allowing Noriko to have her scraps. Maya would take all of Akira, and Noriko was not ready to deal with that since it was so different than what she encountered all this time and out of nowhere (again, the only Akira relationship she was aware of was the one that took years in the making and with her "grown-up" version).

Maya confessed to Akira, which Noriko, despite clearly having sexual inclinations to him didn't do. Maybe out of fear, maybe out of guilt for Niki's descent into suicidal tendencies at home, but the fact of the matter is: she did not present herself as competition, she just let Maya have her way. Perhaps she was shocked Maya was even able to receive a yes. Later, Noriko says that this is the one thing she doesn't envy Maya for, but I'm not sure this is the complete truth. I'll get back into this later.

Some time after the scarf incident, Maya comes to learn about Sekai (probably during sex), and that would end up with her forcing him to abandon Noriko and every connection he had with his past outside of Ami, while at the same time engaging into being a friend to Ami as well (which Noriko was not allowed to do). A year after being ghosted, Noriko sees Akira and Maya (presumably) walking in the old district, gets out of her bus, and confronts them. This is probably when the pact is made, and when Maya regards her as a stalker. This is also Maya definitive win against her (and also possibily when Noriko learns of their sexual relationship).

Now Noriko's in the same position as Niki, with the exception that she never had anything with Akira outside of her pestering him for attention. Basically, her relationship with him is a case of "would things have been different if I..." - the reason why Niki is able to stop looking for him is because they had a relationship in the first place. There isn't much she could have done differently, she was his girlfriend and he chose to not be with her anymore. Noriko though will have to keep wondering for the rest of her life what would have happened if she had pushed more, if she had been different, if she had confessed.

This is when she develops the "I can change myself to suit you" mentality (which is kind of like loser level 2). She behaves this way in the present because of Maya, this is all fueled by the fact that she kept behaving like regular Noriko and that led to what happened. So when she says she doesn't envy being "molested", that's a half-truth, and this is the part that is the half lie. The question of what would have happened if it was her instead has influenced her so much that she thinks is acceptable for her to be cucked by literally everyone, to help each of those people, and be smiling all the while. Because she can't stand the thought of losing again due to her reluctance to take that step.

More could be said about this and how it affects the present, but we can all extrapolate, and it has already been presented. Now to how she's a genius.
Noriko is not a normal girl. I'm not sure about Maya's intellect, but Noriko's definitely not average. Niki points this out a couple of times, and both her grades and level of social interaction attest to how she's able to thrive in multiple spheres of intelligence. And the reason why this is important is because Noriko is able to function in a level that both Niki and Maya can't. Again, Niki, despite being an idol, is kind of a normal girl. She was this geeky teenager that liked anime, playing rpgs and having an older boyfriend.

Look at Noriko. She's this crazy activist that has a job despite not needing one, or even needing to look for one outside of her family restaurant and/or gigs with her sister. She has a good grasp on her teenage angsty and is able to self-evaluate when talking about her political views. She carries a knife glued to her thigh, and has cut herself multiple times because of it, and yet somehow remained so popular in her old school. Noriko is an icon, by which I mean that she's a point outside of the curve.

What is relevant about his however is related to Akira. Noriko is able to understand things the others can't or conveniently ignore. Noriko knows that a better Akira exists and that neither giving up (like Niki did) nor controlling him (like Maya did) will take him there. That is why she keeps searching for him, because she's able to understand that what Maya did fucked him up (probably more in her opinion) than what Sekai did. This is the truth half of her statement. Until Maya had sex with him, Akira was a universal victim - there was no one in the world, including himself, that would judge him harshly, or even at all. It is unclear how much Noriko knows about Sekai (she probably doesn't), but the point remains. Noriko knows that what she did was not such a benevolent act of protection (as Maya likes to convince herself about), and that ultimately this didn't help. Akira stopped having to deal with everything he needs to deal with by using Maya, and by having Maya he began hating himself and isolating himself from any other help by becoming a criminal. Maya only made everything worse.

Maya isn't able to admit this even though it is the truth (and because Maya Prime has the excuse of protecting him from being factory reset), and Niki only realises the truth about her particular situation after Noriko lays the groundwork for it. This is where Noriko's genius really shines through. Noriko understands that she simply doesn't have the tools to help Akira, the only one that can is Niki. Her role is delivering a box that should be opened, and to remind her sister that you can't expect an isolated person to reach out first. A lot of the fanbase likes to attribute Akira's recovery to Niki helping him, but imo it's Noriko's merit. She had to enginner a situation in which both of them would be able to do this, and that would detract to her chances with him. In fact, it would further reinforce how Niki's more relevant than her. Why can Noriko do this then, when Maya wouldn't be able to in a million years? Because Noriko loves him more than either of them? No. I mean, she does love him a lot, but the deciding factor here is that she's smarter.

Whereas Maya and Niki primarily want him, Noriko wants him to recover. When she can point it out, she does it herself, like after Ami cucks her - her conversation with him about how he just let it happen has a lot less to do with her, and a lot more to do with him. Ayane points out to Ami how she takes advantage of Akira and Maya, but it is Noriko that has the balls to tell it to him and to tell him to change. She's the one that sets his recovery in motion with the box of letters, and the one that chooses to make him uncomfortable in the club, even though she knows that is the wrong path to his heart - because, despite what she feels, his heart is not her primary concern. Even when dealing with Maya, Noriko isn't interested in beating her or opening her eyes out of spite, she wants to point out how what she's doing is wrong both to her and to him.

This is the side of Noriko that coupled with her being a loser, makes her the perfect martyr. She's ready and willing to sacrifice herself in order to make Akira healthy. And at times, that approach to things even reminds me of Himawari. The issue about all of this is, unfortunately, that she's insane.
Noriko is not of a sound mind. It is hinted a couple of times that this is the first cycle she had found him, and that those few years felt to her as a lot more. It is my interpretation that this fucked up her brain. While there are things that can be explained by what was previously discussed, some things simply can't. Finding an Akira Arawaka, one of the few remaining men, guardian of an Ami Arakawa, that goes to school in a closed off city is not rocket science. You can add to that their current house possibily being where he lived with Ami at the time he tutored, the fact that Niki is a literal idol and that Noriko could have used some of those connections behind her back, and lastly that Maya didn't change her name either - and yeah, it's either supernatual intervention or bad writing.

Supposing it is an intervention, Noriko is kind of like reverse Maya. Whereas Maya became jaded from spending an eternity fighting the resets by Akira's side, Noriko has been searching for an eternity for him. Mind you, it is hinted that the girls are so into him because it is accumulated from previous cycles - if Noriko has accumulated thousands of years of stalker syndrome it would explain a lot. She literally drugs him during a competition. She is unhinged. And I think that is the main issue with her.

While the loser mentality coupled with the genius trait might have made her the perfect martyr that puts Akira's mental health above her own feelings, and strives for a future that might align her with Himawari's interests, she's also deeply conflicted. While she understands that the correct path for them would be to Akira to fall in love with her for what she is, after managing to recover some of what he is, to eventually being sane enough to choose her as the healthiest option in a bright future - this never works out.

And if she wasn't in love with him, this would be fine. She could have been a more concerned and well-informed Wakana, but instead, she needs his attention, and she needs his love, and what she gets is being constantly cuckholded, and discarded, all the while knowing that if she simply didn't strive for him to be healthier, they'd be fucking all the time. What sucks for Noriko is that I think she's right in her general outlook, but she's a teenager. She doesn't have the maturity to deal with all of this, and neither Akira nor Niki seem interested in her winning. In fact, I think both of them (certainly Niki) want her to give up, because she deserves more, and more importantly, they hope she will be able to grow out of this affection.

Each day, however, we come closer to Noriko breaking. And her breaking would be for her to erase herself, give up on her vision of a better Akira, and simply allow herself to be consumed. At this point, I don't even know if that would be better for her or not. Niki has been awakened by her, and at present is engaged in the "Better Akira project" at a level Noriko simply can't. Akira is getting better too, so it isn't like the plan is failing either. Would her keep postponing sex even matter in the grand scheme of things, or would it just mean that she isn't having sex? I'm curious about her next events, while not expecting much.

and to tell him to change. Noriko is not of a sound mind. It is hinted a couple of times that this is the first cycle she had found him, and that those few years felt to her as a lot more. It is my interpretation that this fucked up her brain. While there are things that can be explained by what was previously discussed, some things simply can't. Finding an Akira Arawaka, one of the few remaining men, guardian of an Ami Arakawa, that goes to school in a closed off city is not rocket science. You can add to that their current house possibily being where he lived with Ami at the time he tutored, the fact that Niki is a literal idol and that Noriko could have used some of those connections behind her back, and lastly that Maya didn't change her name either - and yeah, it's either supernatual intervention or bad writing.
Supposing it is an intervention, Noriko is kind of like reverse Maya. Whereas Maya became jaded from spending an eternity fighting the resets by Akira's side, Noriko has been searching for an eternity for him. a lot
. She literally drugs him during a competition. She is unhinged. And I think that is the main issue with her.

never works out
.

She could have been a more concerned and well-informed Wakana, but instead, she needs his attention, and she needs his love, and what she gets is being constantly cuckholded, and discarded, all the while knowing that if she simply didn't strive for him to be healthier, they'd be fucking all the time. What sucks for Noriko is that I think she's right in her general outlook, but she's a teenager. She doesn't have the maturity to deal with all of this, and neither Akira nor Niki seem interested in her winning. In fact, I think both of them (certainly Niki) want her to give up, because she deserves more, and more importantly, they hope she will be able to grow
out
of this affection.

At this point, I don't even know if that would be better for her or not. Niki has been awakened by her, and at present is engaged in the "Better Akira project" at a level Noriko simply can't. spoilers.title: Loser
spoilers.html:
Noriko's been following Akira since she was born basically and been annoying to him all the while. He complains to Niki that she sticks to him like glue, and she agrees. This doesn't mean that Akira was averse to Noriko rather than just wanting to skip to spending time with Niki, but it does mean that Noriko's relationship with him was from the start her pestering him from attention and getting the scraps he was too pressured to not give her. This is the dynamic that worked for her = pester until he gives something back (which is the seed for stalker behavior).

She was never number one, and she knew she'd never be number one. So her idea of having her love reciprocated was skewed. Sexual awakening for her, which would be being intimate with someone else, was for her to hide in her sister's closet to see Akira being given oral. Not a one time thing either. She didn't wish for him to break up with her sister either, she again, just had to learn to accept whatever fell her way. Understanding this is vital to understanding how Noriko accepted/and still accepts being a loser in love.

Later, when she started being tutored, that was time she could have alone with him in a moment when Akira didn't spend as much time/and later time at all with her sister. That gave her hope she could be number one, especially cause there were other girls being tutored, and of those Noriko most likely was the special one to him. But then the stray arrived. Maya wasn't competing for anything from the start, she didn't have an hour of Akira's time a few days of the week, she lived with him. It was then that Noriko had to see a random girl that came out of nowhere become his number one after each passing week. A girl that was inherently hostile to her btw, different than what Niki was, allowing Noriko to have her scraps. Maya would take all of Akira, and Noriko was not ready to deal with that since it was so different than what she encountered all this time and out of nowhere (again, the only Akira relationship she was aware of was the one that took years in the making and with her "grown-up" version).

Maya confessed to Akira, which Noriko, despite clearly having sexual inclinations to him didn't do. Maybe out of fear, maybe out of guilt for Niki's descent into suicidal tendencies at home, but the fact of the matter is: she did not present herself as competition, she just let Maya have her way. Perhaps she was shocked Maya was even able to receive a yes. Later, Noriko says that this is the one thing she doesn't envy Maya for, but I'm not sure this is the complete truth. I'll get back into this later.

Some time after the scarf incident, Maya comes to learn about Sekai (probably during sex), and that would end up with her forcing him to abandon Noriko and every connection he had with his past outside of Ami, while at the same time engaging into being a friend to Ami as well (which Noriko was not allowed to do). A year after being ghosted, Noriko sees Akira and Maya (presumably) walking in the old district, gets out of her bus, and confronts them. This is probably when the pact is made, and when Maya regards her as a stalker. This is also Maya definitive win against her (and also possibily when Noriko learns of their sexual relationship).

Now Noriko's in the same position as Niki, with the exception that she never had anything with Akira outside of her pestering him for attention. Basically, her relationship with him is a case of "would things have been different if I..." - the reason why Niki is able to stop looking for him is because they had a relationship in the first place. There isn't much she could have done differently, she was his girlfriend and he chose to not be with her anymore. Noriko though will have to keep wondering for the rest of her life what would have happened if she had pushed more, if she had been different, if she had confessed.

This is when she develops the "I can change myself to suit you" mentality (which is kind of like loser level 2). She behaves this way in the present because of Maya, this is all fueled by the fact that she kept behaving like regular Noriko and that led to what happened. So when she says she doesn't envy being "molested", that's a half-truth, and this is the part that is the half lie. The question of what would have happened if it was her instead has influenced her so much that she thinks is acceptable for her to be cucked by literally everyone, to help each of those people, and be smiling all the while. Because she can't stand the thought of losing again due to her reluctance to take that step.

More could be said about this and how it affects the present, but we can all extrapolate, and it has already been presented. Now to how she's a genius.

spoilers.title: Genius

Noriko is not a normal girl. I'm not sure about Maya's intellect, but Noriko's definitely not average. Niki points this out a couple of times, and both her grades and level of social interaction attest to how she's able to thrive in multiple spheres of intelligence. And the reason why this is important is because Noriko is able to function in a level that both Niki and Maya can't. Again, Niki, despite being an idol, is kind of a normal girl. She was this geeky teenager that liked anime, playing rpgs and having an older boyfriend.

Look at Noriko. She's this crazy activist that has a job despite not needing one, or even needing to look for one outside of her family restaurant and/or gigs with her sister. She has a good grasp on her teenage angsty and is able to self-evaluate when talking about her political views. She carries a knife glued to her thigh, and has cut herself multiple times because of it, and yet somehow remained so popular in her old school. Noriko is an icon, by which I mean that she's a point outside of the curve.

What is relevant about his however is related to Akira. Noriko is able to understand things the others can't or conveniently ignore. Noriko knows that a better Akira exists and that neither giving up (like Niki did) nor controlling him (like Maya did) will take him there. That is why she keeps searching for him, because she's able to understand that what Maya did fucked him up (probably more in her opinion) than what Sekai did. This is the truth half of her statement. Until Maya had sex with him, Akira was a universal victim - there was no one in the world, including himself, that would judge him harshly, or even at all. It is unclear how much Noriko knows about Sekai (she probably doesn't), but the point remains. Noriko knows that what she did was not such a benevolent act of protection (as Maya likes to convince herself about), and that ultimately this didn't help. Akira stopped having to deal with everything he needs to deal with by using Maya, and by having Maya he began hating himself and isolating himself from any other help by becoming a criminal. Noriko's been following Akira since she was born basically and been annoying to him all the while. He complains to Niki that she sticks to him like glue, and she agrees. This doesn't mean that Akira was averse to Noriko rather than just wanting to skip to spending time with Niki, but it does mean that Noriko's relationship with him was from the start her pestering him from attention and getting the scraps he was too pressured to not give her. This is the dynamic that worked for her = pester until he gives something back (which is the seed for stalker behavior).

She was never number one, and she knew she'd never be number one. So her idea of having her love reciprocated was skewed. Sexual awakening for her, which would be being intimate with someone else, was for her to hide in her sister's closet to see Akira being given oral. Not a one time thing either. She didn't wish for him to break up with her sister either, she again, just had to learn to accept whatever fell her way. Understanding this is vital to understanding how Noriko accepted/and still accepts being a loser in love.

Later, when she started being tutored, that was time she could have alone with him in a moment when Akira didn't spend as much time/and later time at all with her sister. That gave her hope she could be number one, especially cause there were other girls being tutored, and of those Noriko most likely was the special one to him. But then the stray arrived. Maya wasn't competing for anything from the start, she didn't have an hour of Akira's time a few days of the week, she lived with him. It was then that Noriko had to see a random girl that came out of nowhere become his number one after each passing week. A girl that was inherently hostile to her btw, different than what Niki was, allowing Noriko to have her scraps. Maya would take all of Akira, and Noriko was not ready to deal with that since it was so different than what she encountered all this time and out of nowhere (again, the only Akira relationship she was aware of was the one that took years in the making and with her "grown-up" version).

Maya confessed to Akira, which Noriko, despite clearly having sexual inclinations to him didn't do. Maybe out of fear, maybe out of guilt for Niki's descent into suicidal tendencies at home, but the fact of the matter is: she did not present herself as competition, she just let Maya have her way. Perhaps she was shocked Maya was even able to receive a yes. Later, Noriko says that this is the one thing she doesn't envy Maya for, but I'm not sure this is the complete truth. I'll get back into this later.

Some time after the scarf incident, Maya comes to learn about Sekai (probably during sex), and that would end up with her forcing him to abandon Noriko and every connection he had with his past outside of Ami, while at the same time engaging into being a friend to Ami as well (which Noriko was not allowed to do). A year after being ghosted, Noriko sees Akira and Maya (presumably) walking in the old district, gets out of her bus, and confronts them. This is probably when the pact is made, and when Maya regards her as a stalker. This is also Maya definitive win against her (and also possibily when Noriko learns of their sexual relationship).

Now Noriko's in the same position as Niki, with the exception that she never had anything with Akira outside of her pestering him for attention. Basically, her relationship with him is a case of "would things have been different if I..." - the reason why Niki is able to stop looking for him is because they had a relationship in the first place. There isn't much she could have done differently, she was his girlfriend and he chose to not be with her anymore. Noriko though will have to keep wondering for the rest of her life what would have happened if she had pushed more, if she had been different, if she had confessed.

This is when she develops the "I can change myself to suit you" mentality (which is kind of like loser level 2). She behaves this way in the present because of Maya, this is all fueled by the fact that she kept behaving like regular Noriko and that led to what happened. So when she says she doesn't envy being "molested", that's a half-truth, and this is the part that is the half lie. The question of what would have happened if it was her instead has influenced her so much that she thinks is acceptable for her to be cucked by literally everyone, to help each of those people, and be smiling all the while. Because she can't stand the thought of losing again due to her reluctance to take that step.

More could be said about this and how it affects the present, but we can all extrapolate, and it has already been presented. Now to how she's a genius.
Noriko is not a normal girl. I'm not sure about Maya's intellect, but Noriko's definitely not average. Niki points this out a couple of times, and both her grades and level of social interaction attest to how she's able to thrive in multiple spheres of intelligence. And the reason why this is important is because Noriko is able to function in a level that both Niki and Maya can't. Again, Niki, despite being an idol, is kind of a normal girl. She was this geeky teenager that liked anime, playing rpgs and having an older boyfriend.

Look at Noriko. She's this crazy activist that has a job despite not needing one, or even needing to look for one outside of her family restaurant and/or gigs with her sister. She has a good grasp on her teenage angsty and is able to self-evaluate when talking about her political views. She carries a knife glued to her thigh, and has cut herself multiple times because of it, and yet somehow remained so popular in her old school. Noriko is an icon, by which I mean that she's a point outside of the curve.

What is relevant about his however is related to Akira. Noriko is able to understand things the others can't or conveniently ignore. Noriko knows that a better Akira exists and that neither giving up (like Niki did) nor controlling him (like Maya did) will take him there. That is why she keeps searching for him, because she's able to understand that what Maya did fucked him up (probably more in her opinion) than what Sekai did. This is the truth half of her statement. Until Maya had sex with him, Akira was a universal victim - there was no one in the world, including himself, that would judge him harshly, or even at all. It is unclear how much Noriko knows about Sekai (she probably doesn't), but the point remains. Noriko knows that what she did was not such a benevolent act of protection (as Maya likes to convince herself about), and that ultimately this didn't help. Akira stopped having to deal with everything he needs to deal with by using Maya, and by having Maya he began hating himself and isolating himself from any other help by becoming a criminal. Maya only made everything worse.

Maya isn't able to admit this even though it is the truth (and because Maya Prime has the excuse of protecting him from being factory reset), and Niki only realises the truth about her particular situation after Noriko lays the groundwork for it. This is where Noriko's genius really shines through. Noriko understands that she simply doesn't have the tools to help Akira, the only one that can is Niki. Her role is delivering a box that should be opened, and to remind her sister that you can't expect an isolated person to reach out first. A lot of the fanbase likes to attribute Akira's recovery to Niki helping him, but imo it's Noriko's merit. She had to enginner a situation in which both of them would be able to do this, and that would detract to her chances with him. In fact, it would further reinforce how Niki's more relevant than her. Why can Noriko do this then, when Maya wouldn't be able to in a million years? Because Noriko loves him more than either of them? No. I mean, she does love him a lot, but the deciding factor here is that she's smarter.

Whereas Maya and Niki primarily want him, Noriko wants him to recover. When she can point it out, she does it herself, like after Ami cucks her - her conversation with him about how he just let it happen has a lot less to do with her, and a lot more to do with him. Ayane points out to Ami how she takes advantage of Akira and Maya, but it is Noriko that has the balls to tell it to him and to tell him to change. She's the one that sets his recovery in motion with the box of letters, and the one that chooses to make him uncomfortable in the club, even though she knows that is the wrong path to his heart - because, despite what she feels, his heart is not her primary concern. Even when dealing with Maya, Noriko isn't interested in beating her or opening her eyes out of spite, she wants to point out how what she's doing is wrong both to her and to him.

This is the side of Noriko that coupled with her being a loser, makes her the perfect martyr. She's ready and willing to sacrifice herself in order to make Akira healthy. And at times, that approach to things even reminds me of Himawari. The issue about all of this is, unfortunately, that she's insane.
Noriko is not of a sound mind. It is hinted a couple of times that this is the first cycle she had found him, and that those few years felt to her as a lot more. It is my interpretation that this fucked up her brain. While there are things that can be explained by what was previously discussed, some things simply can't. Finding an Akira Arawaka, one of the few remaining men, guardian of an Ami Arakawa, that goes to school in a closed off city is not rocket science. You can add to that their current house possibily being where he lived with Ami at the time he tutored, the fact that Niki is a literal idol and that Noriko could have used some of those connections behind her back, and lastly that Maya didn't change her name either - and yeah, it's either supernatual intervention or bad writing.

Supposing it is an intervention, Noriko is kind of like reverse Maya. Whereas Maya became jaded from spending an eternity fighting the resets by Akira's side, Noriko has been searching for an eternity for him. Mind you, it is hinted that the girls are so into him because it is accumulated from previous cycles - if Noriko has accumulated thousands of years of stalker syndrome it would explain a lot. She literally drugs him during a competition. She is unhinged. And I think that is the main issue with her.

While the loser mentality coupled with the genius trait might have made her the perfect martyr that puts Akira's mental health above her own feelings, and strives for a future that might align her with Himawari's interests, she's also deeply conflicted. While she understands that the correct path for them would be to Akira to fall in love with her for what she is, after managing to recover some of what he is, to eventually being sane enough to choose her as the healthiest option in a bright future - this never works out.

And if she wasn't in love with him, this would be fine. She could have been a more concerned and well-informed Wakana, but instead, she needs his attention, and she needs his love, and what she gets is being constantly cuckholded, and discarded, all the while knowing that if she simply didn't strive for him to be healthier, they'd be fucking all the time. What sucks for Noriko is that I think she's right in her general outlook, but she's a teenager. She doesn't have the maturity to deal with all of this, and neither Akira nor Niki seem interested in her winning. In fact, I think both of them (certainly Niki) want her to give up, because she deserves more, and more importantly, they hope she will be able to grow out of this affection.

Each day, however, we come closer to Noriko breaking. And her breaking would be for her to erase herself, give up on her vision of a better Akira, and simply allow herself to be consumed. At this point, I don't even know if that would be better for her or not. Niki has been awakened by her, and at present is engaged in the "Better Akira project" at a level Noriko simply can't. Akira is getting better too, so it isn't like the plan is failing either. Would her keep postponing sex even matter in the grand scheme of things, or would it just mean that she isn't having sex? I'm curious about her next events, while not expecting much.

She is a pretty disgusting person, more so than Akira in my opinion.

This might seem like a pretty stupid person, how can a literal child groom an adult person, but that's a misconception that people always have because they assume a young person can never be bad or should never be held accountable.

This is where my moral compass differs from most people, I believe Maya is worse than Akira for the simple reason that her intentions are more ill-purposed than his. She seduced and stole Akira from Niki (presumable using some kind of powers) and made it so that all comunications was ceased between him and the others because "fuck them hes only mine lol"

She doesn't give a fuck about how others feel and only wants him for her selfish desires.

Akira is just a broken man (actions still not justifiable) that finds comfort in getting his Pink-headed yogurt slinger wet from drilling fresh pussy, but he genuinely feels bad for doing it, he's just too weak to control it, and at the end of the way he wishes to help people, that's why he goes out of his way to constatly embark in shenanigans with people. Maya simply doesn't give a fuck about hurting others, that is the big difference.

So if for whatever reason I happened to be WIRES, I would take this stupid bitch and remove her from existance so that she can stop corrupting this shell of infinite power and replace her with a girl that has genuine, un-implanted feelings of love for him. Maybe a girl that can hear sounds.

spoilers.title: Genius
spoilers.html:
Noriko is not a normal girl. I'm not sure about Maya's intellect, but Noriko's definitely not average. Niki points this out a couple of times, and both her grades and level of social interaction attest to how she's able to thrive in multiple spheres of intelligence. And the reason why this is important is because Noriko is able to function in a level that both Niki and Maya can't. Again, Niki, despite being an idol, is kind of a normal girl. She was this geeky teenager that liked anime, playing rpgs and having an older boyfriend.

Look at Noriko. She's this crazy activist that has a job despite not needing one, or even needing to look for one outside of her family restaurant and/or gigs with her sister. She has a good grasp on her teenage angsty and is able to self-evaluate when talking about her political views. She carries a knife glued to her thigh, and has cut herself multiple times because of it, and yet somehow remained so popular in her old school. Noriko is an icon, by which I mean that she's a point outside of the curve.

What is relevant about his however is related to Akira. Noriko is able to understand things the others can't or conveniently ignore. Noriko knows that a better Akira exists and that neither giving up (like Niki did) nor controlling him (like Maya did) will take him there. That is why she keeps searching for him, because she's able to understand that what Maya did fucked him up (probably more in her opinion) than what Sekai did. This is the truth half of her statement. Until Maya had sex with him, Akira was a universal victim - there was no one in the world, including himself, that would judge him harshly, or even at all. It is unclear how much Noriko knows about Sekai (she probably doesn't), but the point remains. Noriko knows that what she did was not such a benevolent act of protection (as Maya likes to convince herself about), and that ultimately this didn't help. Akira stopped having to deal with everything he needs to deal with by using Maya, and by having Maya he began hating himself and isolating himself from any other help by becoming a criminal. Maya only made everything worse.

Maya isn't able to admit this even though it is the truth (and because Maya Prime has the excuse of protecting him from being factory reset), and Niki only realises the truth about her particular situation after Noriko lays the groundwork for it. This is where Noriko's genius really shines through. Noriko understands that she simply doesn't have the tools to help Akira, the only one that can is Niki. Her role is delivering a box that should be opened, and to remind her sister that you can't expect an isolated person to reach out first. A lot of the fanbase likes to attribute Akira's recovery to Niki helping him, but imo it's Noriko's merit. She had to enginner a situation in which both of them would be able to do this, and that would detract to her chances with him. In fact, it would further reinforce how Niki's more relevant than her. Why can Noriko do this then, when Maya wouldn't be able to in a million years? Because Noriko loves him more than either of them? No. I mean, she does love him a lot, but the deciding factor here is that she's smarter.

Whereas Maya and Niki primarily want him, Noriko wants him to recover. When she can point it out, she does it herself, like after Ami cucks her - her conversation with him about how he just let it happen has a lot less to do with her, and a lot more to do with him. Ayane points out to Ami how she takes advantage of Akira and Maya, but it is Noriko that has the balls to tell it to him and to tell him to change. She's the one that sets his recovery in motion with the box of letters, and the one that chooses to make him uncomfortable in the club, even though she knows that is the wrong path to his heart - because, despite what she feels, his heart is not her primary concern. Even when dealing with Maya, Noriko isn't interested in beating her or opening her eyes out of spite, she wants to point out how what she's doing is wrong both to her and to him.

This is the side of Noriko that coupled with her being a loser, makes her the perfect martyr. She's ready and willing to sacrifice herself in order to make Akira healthy. And at times, that approach to things even reminds me of Himawari. The issue about all of this is, unfortunately, that she's insane.

spoilers.title: Insane
spoilers.html:
Noriko is not of a sound mind. It is hinted a couple of times that this is the first cycle she had found him, and that those few years felt to her as a lot more. It is my interpretation that this fucked up her brain. While there are things that can be explained by what was previously discussed, some things simply can't. Finding an Akira Arawaka, one of the few remaining men, guardian of an Ami Arakawa, that goes to school in a closed off city is not rocket science. You can add to that their current house possibily being where he lived with Ami at the time he tutored, the fact that Niki is a literal idol and that Noriko could have used some of those connections behind her back, and lastly that Maya didn't change her name either - and yeah, it's either supernatual intervention or bad writing.

Supposing it is an intervention, Noriko is kind of like reverse Maya. Whereas Maya became jaded from spending an eternity fighting the resets by Akira's side, Noriko has been searching for an eternity for him. Mind you, it is hinted that the girls are so into him because it is accumulated from previous cycles - if Noriko has accumulated thousands of years of stalker syndrome it would explain a lot. She literally drugs him during a competition. She is unhinged. And I think that is the main issue with her.

While the loser mentality coupled with the genius trait might have made her the perfect martyr that puts Akira's mental health above her own feelings, and strives for a future that might align her with Himawari's interests, she's also deeply conflicted. While she understands that the correct path for them would be to Akira to fall in love with her for what she is, after managing to recover some of what he is, to eventually being sane enough to choose her as the healthiest option in a bright future - this never works out.

And if she wasn't in love with him, this would be fine. She could have been a more concerned and well-informed Wakana, but instead, she needs his attention, and she needs his love, and what she gets is being constantly cuckholded, and discarded, all the while knowing that if she simply didn't strive for him to be healthier, they'd be fucking all the time. What sucks for Noriko is that I think she's right in her general outlook, but she's a teenager. She doesn't have the maturity to deal with all of this, and neither Akira nor Niki seem interested in her winning. In fact, I think both of them (certainly Niki) want her to give up, because she deserves more, and more importantly, they hope she will be able to grow out of this affection.

Each day, however, we come closer to Noriko breaking. And her breaking would be for her to erase herself, give up on her vision of a better Akira, and simply allow herself to be consumed. At this point, I don't even know if that would be better for her or not. Niki has been awakened by her, and at present is engaged in the "Better Akira project" at a level Noriko simply can't. Akira is getting better too, so it isn't like the plan is failing either. Would her keep postponing sex even matter in the grand scheme of things, or would it just mean that she isn't having sex? I'm curious about her next events, while not expecting much.

Genius
Noriko is
not
a normal girl. I'm not sure about Maya's intellect, but Noriko's definitely not average. Niki points this out a couple of times, and both her grades and level of social interaction attest to how she's able to thrive in multiple spheres of intelligence. And the reason why this is important is because Noriko is able to function in a level that both Niki and Maya can't. Again, Niki, despite being an idol, is kind of a normal girl. She was this geeky teenager that liked anime, playing rpgs and having an older boyfriend.
Look at Noriko. She's this crazy activist that has a job despite not needing one, or even needing to look for one outside of her family restaurant and/or gigs with her sister. She has a good grasp on her teenage angsty and is able to self-evaluate when talking about her political views. She carries a knife glued to her thigh, and has cut herself multiple times because of it, and yet somehow remained so popular in her old school. Noriko is an icon, by which I mean that she's a point outside of the curve.
What is relevant about his however is related to Akira. Noriko is able to understand things the others can't or conveniently ignore. Noriko knows that a better Akira exists and that neither giving up (like Niki did) nor controlling him (like Maya did) will take him there. That is why she keeps searching for him, because she's able to understand that what Maya did fucked him up (probably more in her opinion) than what Sekai did. This is the truth half of her statement. Until Maya had sex with him, Akira was a universal victim - there was no one in the world, including himself, that would judge him harshly, or even at all. It is unclear how much Noriko knows about Sekai (she probably doesn't), but the point remains. Noriko knows that what she did was not such a benevolent act of protection (as Maya likes to convince herself about), and that ultimately this didn't help. Akira stopped having to deal with everything he needs to deal with by using Maya, and by having Maya he began hating himself and isolating himself from any other help by becoming a criminal. Maya only made everything worse.
Maya isn't able to admit this even though it is the truth (and because Maya Prime has the excuse of protecting him from being factory reset), and Niki only realises the truth about her particular situation
after
Noriko lays the groundwork for it. This is where Noriko's genius really shines through. Noriko understands that she simply doesn't have the tools to help Akira, the only one that can is Niki. Her role is delivering a box that
should be opened
, and to remind her sister that you can't expect an isolated person to reach out first. A lot of the fanbase likes to attribute Akira's recovery to Niki helping him, but imo it's Noriko's merit. She had to enginner a situation in which both of them would be able to do this, and that would detract to her chances with him. In fact, it would further reinforce how Niki's more relevant than her. Why can Noriko do this then, when Maya wouldn't be able to in a million years? Because Noriko loves him more than either of them? When she can point it out, she does it herself, like after Ami cucks her - her conversation with him about how he just let it happen has a lot less to do with her, and a lot more to do with him. Ayane points out to Ami how she takes advantage of Akira and Maya, but it is Noriko that has the balls to tell it
to him
and to tell him to change. She's the one that sets his recovery in motion with the box of letters, and the one that chooses to make him uncomfortable in the club, even though she knows that is the wrong path to his heart - because, despite what she feels, his heart is not her primary concern. Noriko is not of a sound mind. It is hinted a couple of times that this is the first cycle she had found him, and that those few years felt to her as a lot more. It is my interpretation that this fucked up her brain. While there are things that can be explained by what was previously discussed, some things simply can't. Finding an Akira Arawaka, one of the few remaining men, guardian of an Ami Arakawa, that goes to school in a closed off city is not rocket science. You can add to that their current house possibily being where he lived with Ami at the time he tutored, the fact that Niki is a literal idol and that Noriko could have used some of those connections behind her back, and lastly that Maya didn't change her name either - and yeah, it's either supernatual intervention or bad writing.
Supposing it is an intervention, Noriko is kind of like reverse Maya. Whereas Maya became jaded from spending an eternity fighting the resets by Akira's side, Noriko has been searching for an eternity for him. Mind you, it is hinted that the girls are so into him because it is accumulated from previous cycles - if Noriko has accumulated thousands of years of stalker syndrome it would explain
a lot
. She literally drugs him during a competition. She is unhinged. And I think that is the main issue with her.
While the loser mentality coupled with the genius trait might have made her the perfect martyr that puts Akira's mental health above her own feelings, and strives for a future that might align her with Himawari's interests, she's also deeply conflicted. While she understands that the correct path for them would be to Akira to fall in love with her for what she is, after managing to recover some of what he is, to eventually being sane enough to choose her as the healthiest option in a bright future - this
never works out
.

She could have been a more concerned and well-informed Wakana, but instead, she needs his attention, and she needs his love, and what she gets is being constantly cuckholded, and discarded, all the while knowing that if she simply didn't strive for him to be healthier, they'd be fucking all the time. out
of this affection.

And at times, that approach to things even reminds me of Himawari. The issue about all of this is, unfortunately, that she's insane.

spoilers.title: Insane
spoilers.html:
Noriko is not of a sound mind. It is hinted a couple of times that this is the first cycle she had found him, and that those few years felt to her as a lot more. It is my interpretation that this fucked up her brain. While there are things that can be explained by what was previously discussed, some things simply can't. Finding an Akira Arawaka, one of the few remaining men, guardian of an Ami Arakawa, that goes to school in a closed off city is not rocket science. You can add to that their current house possibily being where he lived with Ami at the time he tutored, the fact that Niki is a literal idol and that Noriko could have used some of those connections behind her back, and lastly that Maya didn't change her name either - and yeah, it's either supernatual intervention or bad writing.

Supposing it is an intervention, Noriko is kind of like reverse Maya. Whereas Maya became jaded from spending an eternity fighting the resets by Akira's side, Noriko has been searching for an eternity for him. Mind you, it is hinted that the girls are so into him because it is accumulated from previous cycles - if Noriko has accumulated thousands of years of stalker syndrome it would explain a lot. She literally drugs him during a competition. She is unhinged. And I think that is the main issue with her.

While the loser mentality coupled with the genius trait might have made her the perfect martyr that puts Akira's mental health above her own feelings, and strives for a future that might align her with Himawari's interests, she's also deeply conflicted. While she understands that the correct path for them would be to Akira to fall in love with her for what she is, after managing to recover some of what he is, to eventually being sane enough to choose her as the healthiest option in a bright future - this never works out.

And if she wasn't in love with him, this would be fine. She could have been a more concerned and well-informed Wakana, but instead, she needs his attention, and she needs his love, and what she gets is being constantly cuckholded, and discarded, all the while knowing that if she simply didn't strive for him to be healthier, they'd be fucking all the time. What sucks for Noriko is that I think she's right in her general outlook, but she's a teenager. She doesn't have the maturity to deal with all of this, and neither Akira nor Niki seem interested in her winning. In fact, I think both of them (certainly Niki) want her to give up, because she deserves more, and more importantly, they hope she will be able to grow out of this affection.

Each day, however, we come closer to Noriko breaking. And her breaking would be for her to erase herself, give up on her vision of a better Akira, and simply allow herself to be consumed. At this point, I don't even know if that would be better for her or not. Niki has been awakened by her, and at present is engaged in the "Better Akira project" at a level Noriko simply can't. Akira is getting better too, so it isn't like the plan is failing either. Would her keep postponing sex even matter in the grand scheme of things, or would it just mean that she isn't having sex? I'm curious about her next events, while not expecting much.

A little while back there was some discussion of gods and trees in relation to Kaori's events in the forest and Wires's possible involvement. It turns out that in Chapter 1 there is some pretty strong evidence that trees are connected to all of the trinity, and probably to gods in general.

On the first beach trip, after Sensei begins to disassociate, his inner monologue starts talking about a tree that represents the trinity.





The hex code translates to "trinity". Sensei specifically mentions the branches, leaves, and roots. HOPE's smile is in the branches, right-side up smiles that could represent Pareidolia are in the leaves, and the Wire God's wires are often compared to roots. For example:

During the second reset, Sensei wants HOPE to show up and lead him to roof, and we get another connection to branches:

It's also interesting that Sensei "forgets" what a trunk is called when describing the trinity tree. Here's a few possibilities for what that could mean:
  • It's to call attention to the fact that the other three parts are the important ones.
  • The trunk is what connects everything together, i.e. what combines the trinity into one god. Its name is missing because the trinity is no longer one entity.
  • It represents a currently missing fourth part of the tree, i.e. USER4.

In "Trinity pt. I" three spotlights that almost certainly represent three gods shine on a tree:


Also mildly interesting: the stray cat runs off in response to wind in the tree's branches, both of which are connected to HOPE. It could mean nothing, but maybe it tells us something about Maya's relationship with HOPE.



A connection between gods and trees is also made in "Trinity pt. III" when the "narrator" (probably Pareidolia) goes on a rant against Maya. We're told she's not a god at the same time the text on screen says she's not a tree:

The trinity tree is also referenced by the narrator in the final beach event.





There's some weird stuff happening with the narrator in this event, like the uncharacteristic shift to all caps. Earlier, the narrator directly speaks to Rin, which is the only time I can remember a narrator addressing a non-Sensei character, and Rin seems to hear them, which leads to her hearing things and dreaming about resets in her next few events. The switch to a closeup of the same smile that's in the tree's leaves suggests Pareidolia might be involved, but it seems unlikely that he's the narrator at the beginning of the event.

In any case, whoever the narrator is, they seem to be equating trees to gods again. The "watch me grow" is a direct callback to something HOPE said:

So it seems like the narrator wants both themselves and Sensei to become trees/gods. It's ambiguous as to whether the narrator already is a tree/god, but the wording "watch me grow as if I am a tree" and saying "we can plant ourselves" in future tense makes me think that they aren't yet.

In a later event, the normal narrator directly suggests that Sensei become a god:

One more interesting tree reference is by Tsuneyo when she talks about her dad's love of trees.

This is clearly meant to reference the trinity tree with the inclusion of "the wide part". She doesn't mention roots, the part that is associated with Wires himself, so maybe it's suggesting Wires watching the other gods? But I don't know why they would be the "beautiful things in life", so it probably has another meaning that I'm not seeing.

Returning to Kaori, it unfortunately seems pretty ambiguous who could be acting through the forest. It also re-raises the question of who sent the treasure maps - I think the original consensus was that it was Wires because of his connection to trees? But given Nao's connection to USER4 and the idea that USER4 could be the tree's trunk, maybe it was them instead?

posts.content_html_raw:
DeSkel15 said:
I don't really think someone can be "normal" after watching their parents die
Click to expand...
Of course they can. Normal doesn't really mean nothing bad ever happened to you, just that the things that happened to you don't rule over your life. I never had my parents die in front of me, but a good amount of people have seen people die in front of them and that doesn't have to ruin the rest of their lives for them. Same logic applies to any sort of trauma more or less.

Was the accident very traumatic for Ami? Most certainly. Was the fact that she has received absolutely no professional help, nor a stable home or dependable adult also a problem? Yes, and I would go so far as saying it is even more problematic than her parents dying. Her parents dying was an event that was deeply traumatic, as was when Miku's parents died - but the aftermath was a continued event that went on for years, hasn't stopped and put such a strain on the mind of a kid that it warped her psyque much more than just them dying.

In other words, by not dealing with it in a proper manner, it's like her parents are still dying. Both her and Akira are, in some level, still on that day, they never left. The fact that Akira calls her daughter and she calls him dad is not just important for their interpersonal relationship, but also, in my view, because it starts to manifest the reality that Nozomu is dead. They form a proper family, they grieve and cry together, they bond over their shared trauma and they take control over their life again despite what happened. It would have been much better to do it then, but it's never too late.

Regardless, this is all a minor point - Ami is the way she is because things were done in the way they were. We'll all just continue hoping she can get as healthy as she can now that Akira's taking responsabilty.

Her parents dying was an event that was deeply traumatic, as was when Miku's parents died - but the aftermath was a continued event that went on for years, hasn't stopped and put such a strain on the mind of a kid that it warped her psyque much more than just them dying.
In other words, by not dealing with it in a proper manner, it's like her parents are still dying. Both her and Akira are, in some level, still on that day, they never left. The fact that Akira calls her daughter and she calls him dad is not just important for their interpersonal relationship, but also, in my view, because it starts to manifest the reality that Nozomu is dead. They form a proper family, they grieve and cry together, they bond over their shared trauma and they take control over their life again despite what happened. It would have been much better to do it then, but it's never too late.
Regardless, this is all a minor point - Ami is the way she is because things were done in the way they were. We'll all just continue hoping she can get as healthy as she can now that Akira's taking responsabilty.

So I'm basically fucked then lol

Also, I may be on the minority, but I believe LiL will have a happy ending. However, we need to understand what we mean by happy.
There are basically four ways a story can end, they are divided by if the overall objective was reached, and the main character's feelings about this (or sometimes the reader's). Basically, let's say the story was about Akira becoming a good person - well, if by the end he did then it's a success, if he didn't, then it's a failure. However, it could also be that him becoming a good person is a bad thing for him, because he learns that he's dead and can only lament it was already too late. Or, not being able to change is a good thing for him, because he fully accepts who he is and finds peace in living forever in a made-up world.

Who knows what we'll discover, I just mean that even if the ending is tragic (which I don't believe it has to be), even then it can be happy. For instance, being able to make peace with his life and loved ones before finally concluding his fall from a building would be happy, in a strange sort of way.

I am aiming for Akira exits the simulation and smiles though, he doesn't even have to end up with anyone, just him alive and being able to smile again would be great (Ayane has to be pregnant though because Himawari has to be protected).

Regarding purity routes, joking aside, I fully understand if Maya's the last one (or maybe she doesn't even have one) - it seems to be the most important. At this point in time, other than Ayane and Ami (for supernatural reasons) I'd like to see Yumi's purity route most of all. There was something going on between the two even before the resets, and I think it would be interesting to see to which extent Akira was aiming to either groom her, or the very opposite, trying to give her actual help in the sense of what he'd have liked to have been given instead of a Sekai.

But I guess we'll probably find that out before the purity routes.

Edit: I'm not dying until this shit's finished. I want to see the ending.

spoilers.text:
There are basically four ways a story can end, they are divided by if the overall objective was reached, and the main character's feelings about this (or sometimes the reader's). Basically, let's say the story was about Akira becoming a good person - well, if by the end he did then it's a success, if he didn't, then it's a failure. However, it could also be that him becoming a good person is a bad thing for him, because he learns that he's dead and can only lament it was already too late. Or, not being able to change is a good thing for him, because he fully accepts who he is and finds peace in living forever in a made-up world.
Who knows what we'll discover, I just mean that even if the ending is tragic (which I don't believe it has to be), even then it can be happy. For instance, being able to make peace with his life and loved ones before finally concluding his fall from a building would be happy, in a strange sort of way.
I am aiming for Akira exits the simulation and smiles though, he doesn't even have to end up with anyone, just him alive and being able to smile again would be great (Ayane has to be pregnant though because Himawari has to be protected).

If she needs a blackmail that doesn't put him in jail, she could simply say she'll get him fired and without money (in her view) he can't provide for Ami.

It doesn't really fit that she would have Akira have sex with Touka/Tsukasa/Yasu for blackmail, or even amusement for that matter (because she overall seemed to want to manipulate things to a "better" outcome, like she's a matriarch fixing people's lives without them knowing). Her rationale of "let's have Touka have her heart broken in a 'safe' manner, by falling in love with someone I can control and therefore won't be harmful to the family", while bizarre, follows logic.

Her putting Tsukasa in danger on a whim does not. I think that's where most people started scratching their heads. You can argue that Touka has enough maturity to choose for herself to pursue a sexual relationship (while still a crime), but Tsukasa absolutely does not. So what is this about? Is she trying to "help" Akira by putting him into a situation that he fears, and then proving he's able to control himself? Why would she care though, and why risk her daughter in doing so? Tsukasa may be "disposable", but even then it doesn't fit that Tsubasa wouldn't care about having one of her daughters sexually assaulted while being a kid (if anything for her family reputation of having to deal with a broken person). Also, I don't really buy into Tsukasa's view of her mother not caring about her - cause if she didn't, she wouldn't put up with Tsukasa as much as she does.

In fact, about Tsukasa specifically, I'm not saying her problems aren't real, they certainly are. But you can view it from the other side: Touka has to deal with all the pressure of being the heir (and being a woman when they wanted a man). Tsukasa has been freed from that. What she views as neglect is also a privilege. It's both things, and that's why it makes it even harder for Tsubasa to deal with it, since the one that has all the responsability thrust upon her (Touka) behaves as a sane person, while the one that doesn't have responsabilities behaves as a brat. You can see the gap between how the two of them view the same situation when Tsubasa has Akira in her office and Tsukasa yells at her. She calls off the meeting and seems honestly hurt by the situation, following it by going after her supposed "spare".

Tangent aside, I hope Tsubasa is being influenced by the tree or has another angle, because her actions since the Tsukasa thing stopped making sense for me, and for a lot of people I'd wager.

But you can view it from the other side: Touka has to deal with all the pressure of being the heir (and being a woman when they wanted a man). Tsukasa has been freed from that. What she views as neglect is also a privilege. It's both things, and that's why it makes it even harder for Tsubasa to deal with it, since the one that has all the responsability thrust upon her (Touka) behaves as a sane person, while the one that doesn't have responsabilities behaves as a brat. You can see the gap between how the two of them view the same situation when Tsubasa has Akira in her office and Tsukasa yells at her. She calls off the meeting and seems honestly hurt by the situation, following it by going after her supposed "spare".
Tangent aside, I hope Tsubasa is being influenced by the tree or has another angle, because her actions since the Tsukasa thing stopped making sense for me, and for a lot of people I'd wager.
Click to expand...
It's not about
needing
blackmail. It's about having the power to make it.
Tsukasa is definitely just a spare, though. She's valuable in that she's the only spare, but a spare nevertheless.
There's a reason AUTO-PILOT noted that Tsubasa has corrupting sludge in her veins, and Tsukasa is disposable:
Spoiler
Narrator/AUTO-PILOT - "She didn't have much experience with lying, but she didn't
need
it as she had acquired the skill at birth."
- "You see, her mother was exceptional at it. So exceptional that her daughters still believed her to be pure of heart despite the organ pumping sludge through her veins on a near constant basis."
- "It was this sludge that was passed on to her daughters. And while it had not fully corrupted them yet, it was sure to do so over time."
- "Another truth is that the young one was disposable. There was no need for a second child in the Tsukioka family. Their existence was naught more than a failsafe should the eldest perish."
(Chapter 4's 'You & Me Against The World' Main Event)
Tsukasa is, of course, far more valuable than any Non-Tsukioka (besides maybe the more interesting ones like Sensei), but she's still just a failsafe. Tsubasa only seems to truly care about the "greater good":
Spoiler
Tsubasa - "For the greater good, of course. That greater good being
us
."
(Chapter 4's 'You & Me Against The World' Main Event)
Presumably her and Touka, in particular.
Sensei probably just entertains Tsubasa like Yasu or Tsuneyo entertains him. Or like Tsubasa put it:
Spoiler
Tsubasa - "Akira, Akira, Akira...What an
interesting
man you are."
(Chapter 4's Tsubasa 'The Bird & The Worm' Event)
He's
interesting
. Tsukasa is presumably being used as a way to make him more so.

There were a couple of things that I intended to include in this post but forgot about, so I'll add them on here.
Pareidolia (or maybe SekaiDolia?) seems to affect Sensei or at least is referenced in a lot of Futaba's events. Some of these could be coincidence or just Sensei's broken mind, but there's definitely enough here to establish a pattern (and I easily might have missed some, this wasn't initially something I was looking for). Some open-ended observations related to "Bluejay" that I mostly don't know what to make of:

Something which I've noticed that Selebus likes to do as an evasion is to have a character say something with a clear surface-level meaning but which is actually ambiguous, then have someone explicitly state the surface-level meaning without actually resolving the initial meaning. With that in mind, I suspect that Makoto's talk of seeing "over the barrier" here has a deeper intended meaning, but I have no suggestions as to what.
Makoto talks about seeing better with your eyes closed, which Sensei recognizes as something the narrator (or Pareidolia) told him on the beach while talking about the trinity tree. This is interesting for a couple of reasons. First, it means that, whether it's conscious or not, Sensei can apparently hear and remember at least some of what the narrator is saying. Second, it might establish a link between Makoto and whoever was talking on the beach.




Makoto apparently doesn't decide to bluejay herself until Sensei starts describing the rooftop apocalypse.


Makoto doesn't gain Sensei's trauma/wishing well eyes immediately after her suicide is reset, so apparently something more happens after she goes home for the night?
The next day, someone (the narrator? Pareidolia? Sensei's internal monologue?) finishes Makoto's sentence to say that "nothing is real", and given that she never finishes the sentence herself, she might somehow be aware of it happening.

spoilers.title: Bluejay
spoilers.html:
Some open-ended observations related to "Bluejay" that I mostly don't know what to make of:

Something which I've noticed that Selebus likes to do as an evasion is to have a character say something with a clear surface-level meaning but which is actually ambiguous, then have someone explicitly state the surface-level meaning without actually resolving the initial meaning. With that in mind, I suspect that Makoto's talk of seeing "over the barrier" here has a deeper intended meaning, but I have no suggestions as to what.
Makoto talks about seeing better with your eyes closed, which Sensei recognizes as something the narrator (or Pareidolia) told him on the beach while talking about the trinity tree. This is interesting for a couple of reasons. First, it means that, whether it's conscious or not, Sensei can apparently hear and remember at least some of what the narrator is saying. Second, it might establish a link between Makoto and whoever was talking on the beach.




Makoto apparently doesn't decide to bluejay herself until Sensei starts describing the rooftop apocalypse.


Makoto doesn't gain Sensei's trauma/wishing well eyes immediately after her suicide is reset, so apparently something more happens after she goes home for the night?
The next day, someone (the narrator? Pareidolia? Sensei's internal monologue?) finishes Makoto's sentence to say that "nothing is real", and given that she never finishes the sentence herself, she might somehow be aware of it happening.

Dc345 said:
On the topic of rape does, Tsubasa want Sensei to rape her/Niki her(reffering to Otoha cuck scene)? She keeps meddling in Sensei's affairs and when he tells her to stop she asks if there are any consequences. Could this be her pushing Sensei to the point where he gets fed up to the point where he has her way with her?
Click to expand...
I don't think so, and there are two parts about this.

First is that, Tsubasa should be someone that needs to or tries to constantly think several steps ahead to bring any potential benefit to the people she cares, and Sensei is likely not one of them. A series of button pushing is an effort to understand where Sensei and her daughters currently are in her imaginative roadmap, what direction they might move on from there, whether she agrees with the benefits that direction could bring to her daughters or not, and whether a nudge on her end is necessary to accelerate or course-correct.

I think there is always some amount of honest excitement when dealing with Sensei due to perhaps knowing what he does with Chika, and perhaps due to natural attraction to a hot dude. But this is far from being the determining factor to her actions in the face of her duty as the puppeteer. Any attempt in explaining this otherwise as a kink or a villainous hobby is currently too weak. Even if Tsubasa herself claims to have askew moral code, I choose to believe that it's the mean to an end that is askew and not the end. Essentially, wanting to see something spicy or wanting some of that dick herself shouldn't be your first guess.

Second is that, according to her life trajectory and realistically speaking, Tsubasa will not receive consequence and she herself should be the believer of that. It requires balls bigger than Selly's ego to forgo everything and pork the most influential woman in the city even at a fit of rage. It doesn't mean she has plot armor; it just means that she thinks she does, and thus there is a high chance that what ends up happening might not be exactly what she hoped for or what she seemed to be going for. And this I think is an ongoing theme that revolves around Tsubasa whenever Sensei is involved: she is not just playing with fire against her best judgement or thinking she always gets the upper hand; she is playing with fire without knowing that's a fire.

This feeling is especially strong when it comes to her plans with Tsukasa. I generally think Tsubasa may or may not fully believe Sensei's wariness about being around wizards, and is still trying her best to move Tsukasa's case forward in a good direction, but this time it's exceptionally difficult to make the right choice even for her. You might say "just find another tutor that's not a proven pedophile" and you'd be absolutely right. However, from Tsubasa's perspective, she needs someone with experience, enough intelligence, a spine that can withstand Tsukasa's BS, amongst other things that relate more to mentally growing her girls up and less to do with just education. She might believe that she can still nudge Sensei and Tsukasa into the right direction against all odds, but backfiring is very imminent and almost unavoidable only from a god's perspective.

Someone liking a story is totally subjective, yes, but discussing if the story makes sense not so much. The way our discussions tend to go in saying something is bad or not is if it makes sense with what has been presented so far or not (aka narrative cohesion).

A big topic of discussion has been something that happened on update 0.39, regarding many characters seemingly ignoring one character's actions when it would make more sense for them to be more bothered about it. In the same token, one of the big topics of discussion for the next update is what a certain character may react as, and in how many ways it would make sense for her to react. None of these are based in how we'd like things to go (although obviously that's a part of it), but more what would make sense to happen.

That said, I agree with you that even the fact we can have these discussions is so far removed from what one would expect from an adult game that it remains as a testament to Selebus' ability as a storyteller. On that specific front, I have great praise for him.

posts.content_html_raw:
95vengeancef said:
Who can tell how many religious and occult elements the game contains, and how many "new weird" there are?
Click to expand...
Religious elements tend to focus around christian symbolism, presumably because of Akira's family. Bible quotes, crosses, angels, general moralism around sin, even the notion of 3 gods being 1. One could argue that the eternal struggle between light and dark with humanity being the rope in between them is from Manichaeism, but that has been since incorporated into christianity so I guess it's nitpicking. That would be the same for most of the random elements that are thrown around.

Occult elements are hard to pinpoint because what is presented doesn't necessarily refer to any specific occult element rather than having an occult feel to it. "The old one" for instance (and even NAO), could simply be Selebus' creation, rather than a Lovecraftian reference. Same goes for the sakura trees and the world itself - and to a larger extent, things like wires, semen and voices in your head seem to be very much a Selebus "creation" rather than a specific reference to something. Of those there are countless, and for an example of what I mean: You could find numerous references of secrets hidden in the wind or in the voice of cicadas in occult literature, but to say Selebus is making a direct reference to one of them would be forcing the point imo. It doesn't seem to be the case.

There is also random stuff that he throws in that I don't think merit a real analysis. You could argue that Flora, the Emissary of Pegasus, the Council of Plants, the Untitled tv show, and so on, have counterparts in movie and literature culture as a whole. But to each their own in terms of what to delve into.

You haven't asked, but it is important to note that although there aren't many specific occult references, there are many poetry ones. Those tend to be blatant enough that you'd recognize them though, so if anything sounds like classic poetry to you there is a likely chance Selebus is referencing something.

There are a few references to architectural landmarks, paintings, movies and videogames too - but those are in the extreme minority. Strangely enough, I don't remember many references to literature novels though (I can only recall "where the sidewalk ends", but even that is not exactly classic literature, as he tends to use classic poetry). I guess Akira's deal really was poetry...
