Moonflare said:
Religious elements tend to focus around christian symbolism, presumably because of Akira's family. Bible quotes, crosses, angels, general moralism around sin, even the notion of 3 gods being 1. One could argue that the eternal struggle between light and dark with humanity being the rope in between them is from Manichaeism, but that has been since incorporated into christianity so I guess it's nitpicking. That would be the same for most of the random elements that are thrown around.

Occult elements are hard to pinpoint because what is presented doesn't necessarily refer to any specific occult element rather than having an occult feel to it. "The old one" for instance (and even NAO), could simply be Selebus' creation, rather than a Lovecraftian reference. Same goes for the sakura trees and the world itself - and to a larger extent, things like wires, semen and voices in your head seem to be very much a Selebus "creation" rather than a specific reference to something. Of those there are countless, and for an example of what I mean: You could find numerous references of secrets hidden in the wind or in the voice of cicadas in occult literature, but to say Selebus is making a direct reference to one of them would be forcing the point imo. It doesn't seem to be the case.

There is also random stuff that he throws in that I don't think merit a real analysis. You could argue that Flora, the Emissary of Pegasus, the Council of Plants, the Untitled tv show, and so on, have counterparts in movie and literature culture as a whole. But to each their own in terms of what to delve into.

You haven't asked, but it is important to note that although there aren't many specific occult references, there are many poetry ones. Those tend to be blatant enough that you'd recognize them though, so if anything sounds like classic poetry to you there is a likely chance Selebus is referencing something.

There are a few references to architectural landmarks, paintings, movies and videogames too - but those are in the extreme minority. Strangely enough, I don't remember many references to literature novels though (I can only recall "where the sidewalk ends", but even that is not exactly classic literature, as he tends to use classic poetry). I guess Akira's deal really was poetry...

Sekai is Amis mother.She was our brothers wife.Now while we cant be 100% sure that Ami is our brothers child and not ours lets say that its our brothers.Sekai i believe is the reason why sensei is the way he is.At the very least she is what started all of this.
My understanding of Sekais role in all of this is this.Sekai,being the depraved person that she is,use Akira as her muse in order to write her poems(Her pen name was "The girl who drowned" and As wakana so elequently put it~
So its safe to assume that Sekai was a disgusting depraved person that used Akira as her outlet for those exact impulses.Now if we use some basic psycology,i believe we all can imagine how years upom years of being abused in more ways than one would change a person.The result of that is the Akira we see today.Fast forward to the time where Akira was a tutor on that disgusting shell of a building.
His students were Maya and Noriko.They both loved him dearly and he taught them everything they know but as it always goes hostility was developed between the 2.At the end of her rope Maya made a sort of promise,a pact you can say,with Noriko to split the city in half.Norikos half of the city was the old District,while Mayas was what remained.Of course that pact didnt last long and Noriko became,as Maya said,a disgusting stalker that needs to die right this instant.Now,based on Akiras trauma and as a result his attraction to teenagers(And of course an off-hand comment by Noriko that Maya got molested((Which i cant find rn so if anyone could help i would appreciate it))something along the lines of~
Maya,a young and immature kid not knowing better threw herself at Akira and he of course being the broken man that he is took advantage of that.That was what truly solidified their relationship and what sparked Mayas possessive and control freak tendencies that we see her exhibit from the moment Noriko appeared.Now i still dont know why the Green scarf was such a momumental item for Maya(Enough to make her break down for a bit) but judging by the fact that it "Appeared out of nowhere" ill just say that its either the world fucking with her(as always) OR something happened in the winter in the past and that marked it as a special item for her.(PS the second time this scarf appeared the saleswoman was the shapeshifter)
Thats pretty much Akiras character,and subsequent trauma summarized.

Comiies, DeSkel thrives in setting timelines for the sort of stuff you're discussing, and he actually played Nothing is Beautiful (I just read about it). I'll contribute what I can before he arrives though:
Yuu and Saki are Akira's parents. You meet Saki during the first reset and she says she's looking for Yuu. Saki was a deeply religious person, this is referenced by Yasu and Akira himself. Yuu was troubled, and Pareidolia says during the Spring reset that if Akira doesn't get a grip he'll end up like Yuu. We take this to mean that Yuu lost himself to his mental sickness somehow (but it isn't confirmed).

Akira has had blackouts way before the resets, this has to do with his mental sickness (that should have been inherited from Yuu), and one of the theories as to why Saki didn't like him is because he reminded her too much of her husband (by hearing voices and stuff like that) - what supports this theory is that she'd sneak into his bed sometimes at night, and cry while hugging him. This would also align with Ami being his daughter and hearing voices because she too has the same mental illness. Again, this is a theory, the only thing that's certain is that he had blackouts before the resets (none of this necessarily excludes supernatural elements btw).

The memories of Sekai explain in her second class that she tried everything to find happiness, but only found it after "falling in love" with Akira. So Nozomu doesn't seem to have been a means to get to Akira, she first molests him when she's already Nozomu's wife and Akira falls from a window - she offers to stay at home to care for him. However, it's very possible that she stayed with Nozomu after that to maintain her connection to Akira. As for Nozomu, he at least suspected their relationship (Ami points out that he'd get angry when Akira talked about Sekai's scent), and it's possible that the car crash was caused by him confronting Sekai about it (see First Contact, when someone says "why did it have to be him?").

We know close to nothing about Nozomu. Ami regards him as "normal", Saki at the very least disliked him less than Akira, he was jealous either about Sekai or Akira, he may have been gay and forced to abandon his sexuality and turned this into molesting teenagers and being the father to some of the girls (there's a whole theory about this applying to him or Akira, which I do not subscribe to). And his name might not have been Nozomu, as Sekai's name might not have been that as well - since both of these names differ from regular names used and Nozomu can be translated as Hope, and Sekai as World. Again, most about him are theories without much substance.

On Sekai though, there's a lot to be said - but it is vital to point out that we don't have confirmation about ever meeting Sekai. We meet Akira's memories of her. From what we see, she seems to believe she only loved two things in her life, that being Ami and Akira, in that order. We find out that she did not have a good relationship with her parents and did not use her family name (Karin's father explains this). Sekai seemed to be a teacher (probably of English) for younger students. She may have faked believing in god as a crutch for Ami to deal with her mental issues (same as what Saki did for Akira).

It is highly debatable if Sekai actually loved Akira, from a recent scene of them talking while sitting on a table overlooked by the moon - she says they'll travel the world, and if we were to believe her, she may have had plans to leave Nozomu to be with him and Ami. Akira seemed to never buy into that, and neither do I. We will never know because, obviously, she died before having the chance. So unless she was breaking up with Nozomu on the day of the accident, she never tried to overturn her relationship with Akira into something healthier.

There's a lot more to be said, but this is a good start. Regarding Maya and Noriko, Akira first met Maya while wandering around and bought her coffee. That was the day she ran away from her home after being sexually abused. This probably happened after Sekai's death. At the very least it was close to it because, in the earliest memory we see of them in the tutoring place, he hasn't met Niki for months. Meaning he stopped seeing her but it wasn't years yet.

Noriko was the one that got jealous, but she dealt with it much better than Maya. Noriko saw Akira about two times a week, but Maya started living with him. She had nothing else, she abandoned her own life and entrusted it to a stranger. We do know that she was the one that confessed to him and he did not accept her at first.

The scarf stuff was about the night he finally accepted her and they became a thing. When Himawari sells the scarf to Akira, it's the exact scarf (through supernatural means) which makes Maya break down because she has had to supress her feelings for so long. That makes her start to accept that this Akira is the actual Akira. There are theories as to why Himawari (and whoever she was working for at the time) had to have Maya accept that this Akira is the Akira. And the scarf was definitely a big step in that direction.

Chika's and Chinami's father abandons them at some point, (if he was ever around) leaving their mother Chiaki to figure things out.

Uta has likely started sharing nudes with pedos by now, and at some point, her family finds out, and her brother tries to kill one of her stalkers, then ends up incarcerated.
8 year old Yasu predicts the world ending (presumably referring to Sekai and the accident), then starts getting taken advantage of by her doctor.
Yumi's mother has likely abandoned her, by now.

Around 10 year old Nodoka publishes her first book. Presumably is taking care of her mother, who can't really function on her own, by now. Possibly befriended and started defending Futaba around this time.
Chika's and Chinami's mother had presumably died around this time. Chika then likely finds work, gets held back in school, and probably meets the likes of Yumi and Rin afterwards.

Chika, Chinami, and Yumi likely became like a found family, by now.
Futaba and Nodoka have likely became close friends by now.
Futaba and Rin likely become like sisters, around/by this time.

Kirin had likely lost to Ayane at a science fair, and also probably became "friends" by this point.
Kirin has likely became close friends with Miku, by now.
Nodoka and Otoha become close friends, for some reason.
Niki had became suicidal, wasted most of her 20s on Sensei, then gets scouted and becomes an Idol, around this time.
Noriko had begun her search for Sensei, and almost finds him in the Old District once.
Sensei becomes or is becoming a Teacher around this time. (While hiding his relationship with Maya from everyone)
Uta, in an effort to escape her stalkers, is sent by her family to live with her grandpa in Kumon-mi, who slowly dies. She probably becomes a Maid around this time.
Uta and Io have likely became close friends by now.
The Space War happens around 2017/16, and the majority of men are C̶u̶l̶l̶e̶d̶ sent to space. (May be related to the end of tutoring, and Sensei and Maya ghosting Noriko, but it's not clear)
Most marriages and relationships have likely been formed, by now.

By Long Maya:

(Chapter 3's 'Untitled' Main Event)
Uta:

(Chapter 4's Tsuneyo 'Soothsayer' Event)

Sensei becomes the Teacher for all the girls on the first floor, and teaches them for a few months.
Ami, Ayane, Futaba, Maya, Molly, Rin, and Sana, join/create the Manga Club, and Sensei becomes the Manga Club's adviser.
Futaba and Makoto begin to admire Sensei. (And probably crush on him)
Maya and Sensei presumably have secret meetings on the roof, and continue to hide their relationship.
Yumi bullies others, especially Futaba, and ends up getting creepy detentions and stalked by Sensei.
Yumi and creepy Sensei:
Spoiler
Yumi - "You think I just up and forgot about all those fucking creepy ass detentions?! Get real!"
(Chapter 1's Yumi 'Five Million Dollars' Event)
- "Shit, dude. You even tracked me down at the arcade a few times and made it so I can't even chill
there
anymore."
(Chapter 1's 'Not Even Me' Main Event)
Kaori presumably gets out of the hospital at some point.
Months into the school year, the Resets apparently begin.
Tsuneyo's father seemingly gets sick and she has to go to school around this time.
Tsuneyo had only been going to school for weeks, after her father got sick, which seems to be around when the game starts and maybe when the Resets did:
Spoiler

- "I was homeschooled until recently."
- "But my father has become sick and now I must rely on Ms. Watabe."
(Chapter 1's 'Tsuneyo Tojo, Stand-up Comedian' Main Event)
Maya presumably makes it to the roof and survives the first Reset, and every Reset since. (This is later proved false by an Ami who reveals that she's been around longer and that Maya has been reset many times over millions and millions of years)
Seemingly, millions of years and hundreds of thousands of iterations of Sensei and the girls occur.
Long Maya implies their show has been "on the air" for millions of years:
Spoiler
Long Maya - "I'd like to take another moment to thank our guest for sharing his thoughts with us- and our sponsors for keeping this show on the air for several million years now!"
('Good boy' Happy Event)
Maya implies there's been hundreds of thousands of Sensei's:
Spoiler
Maya - "I mean...Would you be able to handle the memories of hundreds of thousands of lifetimes if they were to all rush in at once?"
(Chapter 1's Maya 'Takoyaki' Event)
And implies each new Sensei reformats the girls:
Spoiler
Maya - "What you were witnessing in those moments were their memories being rewritten."
- "What you were experiencing in watching those girls adapt to you was a type of reformatting."
(Chapter 2's Maya 'Now More Than Ever' Event)
Himawari/The Shapeshifter was presumably created at some point.
Maya claims to have spent centuries trying to tell Ami about the resets, which she now considers a bad idea, due to how it apparently affected Ami. (Maya claims that, before any transfers, Ami has butchered and broke everyone after being triggered, at some point. Besides Maya presumably)
Maya creates and places a journal in Sensei's room to help stop any New Sensei from immediately failing on day one. (Likely placed many other things in his room as well)
Sensei:
Becomes aware of the Resets at some point.
Never survived the 3rd Reset or made it past Winter, changed personalities a lot, and is implied to have been "broken" many times by Maya, according to Maya.
Seemed to break and rape the girls more often than not.
Chapter 1 seems to start around here.
May have missed some things. This game is huge.

spoilers.html:
• "It started"
According to Possessed Tsuneyo:
Tsuneyo(?) - "There are clues in a house near a lake. It started before you were born."
(Chapter 4's Tsuneyo 'TH15 15NT M3' Event)
  • Yasu's religion goes back 200+ years at least.
According to Touka:
Touka - "It appears that Yasu's beliefs are either derivative of or an exact replication of a religion that used to be practiced in Kumon-mi long before any of us were born."
- "It's been nearly two-hundred years since it's shown up in text. But the few text accounts we were able to scrounge up mirror what she says almost one-to-one."
(Chapter 4's 'Priestess of Fallen Snow' Main Event)
  • The Everblooming Sakura Tree and the Tsukioka Family go back centuries, and to the origins of Kumon-mi.
According to Tsubasa:
Tsubasa - "The Tsukioka family is one dating back to the origins of Kumon-mi, and this garden has been mostly untouched for all of it's history."
- "We'll cap off today's portion of the tour with our indoor arboretum- another family relic that's been an important part of our history for centuries."
- "A long time ago, before industrialization took up its scythe and laid waste to our lands, Kumon-mi was covered in trees and filled with wildlife."
- "This 'arboretum' hold but one tree- an everblooming sakura, kept alive by extremely specific climate controlling, imported soil, and a fair bit of wilpower."
- "Just think of how much this tree has seen. All of those stories I recounted for you today would be actual memories for something that's been alive as long as our sakura."
(Chapter 2's Tsubasa 'Everbloom (Pride of The Sinful Sort)' Event)
  • Birth of everyone older than Sensei:
    • His Parents (and those of their generation)
    • His Brother, Nozomu
    • Sekai
    • Tsubasa
    • Rika (Around 1977 assuming she's 43)
    • Yuki
    • Etc
  • Birth of everyone a few years older than Sensei:
    • Haruka (Around 1986)
    • Maki (Around 1986)
    • Sara (Around 1987)
    • Etc
  • Presumably whatever happens in 'Nothing is Beautiful' happens.
    • Yuu's mother dies of cancer. (Presumably Sensei's grandmother, if Yuu is his father)
    • Saki's family is murdered. (Presumably Sensei's mother's side of the family, if this Saki is his Saki)
  • Sensei is born 31 years ago around 1989.

- "But my father has become sick and now I must rely on Ms. Watabe."

    • Seemed to break and rape the girls more often than not.

DeSkel15 said:
Here's a little timeline for those interested (doesn't cover everything, but should help one get the gist):

Before Sensei (Before 1989):
  • "It started"
According to Possesed Tsuneyo:
View attachment 3768950 Tsuneyo(?) - "There are clues in a house near a lake. It started before you were born."
(Chapter 4's Tsuneyo 'TH15 15NT M3' Event)
  • Yasu's religion goes back 200+ years at least.
According to Touka:
View attachment 3768967 View attachment 3768968 Touka - "It appears that Yasu's beliefs are either derivative of or an exact replication of a religion that used to be practiced in Kumon-mi long before any of us were born."
- "It's been nearly two-hundred years since it's shown up in text. But the few text accounts we were able to scrounge up mirror what she says almost one-to-one."
(Chapter 4's 'Priestess of Fallen Snow' Main Event)
  • The Everblooming Sakura Tree and the Tsukioka Family go back centuries, and to the origins of Kumon-mi.
According to Tsubasa:
View attachment 3769249 View attachment 3769032 View attachment 3769247 View attachment 3769039 View attachment 3769248 Tsubasa - "The Tsukioka family is one dating back to the origins of Kumon-mi, and this garden has been mostly untouched for all of it's history."
- "We'll cap off today's portion of the tour with our indoor arboretum- another family relic that's been an important part of our history for centuries."
- "A long time ago, before industrialization took up its scythe and laid waste to our lands, Kumon-mi was covered in trees and filled with wildlife."
- "This 'arboretum' hold but one tree- an everblooming sakura, kept alive by extremely specific climate controlling, imported soil, and a fair bit of wilpower."
- "Just think of how much this tree has seen. All of those stories I recounted for you today would be actual memories for something that's been alive as long as our sakura."
(Chapter 2's Tsubasa 'Everbloom (Pride of The Sinful Sort)' Event)
  • Birth of everyone older than Sensei:
    • His Parents (and those of their generation)
    • His Brother, Nozomu
    • Sekai
    • Tsubasa
    • Rika (Around 1977 assuming she's 43)
    • Yuki
    • Etc
  • Birth of everyone a few years older than Sensei:
    • Haruka (Around 1986)
    • Maki (Around 1986)
    • Sara (Around 1987)
    • Etc
  • Presumably whatever happens in 'Nothing is Beautiful' happens.
    • Yuu's mother dies of cancer. (Presumably Sensei's grandmother, if Yuu is his father)
    • Saki's family is murdered. (Presumably Sensei's mother's side of the family, if this Saki is his Saki)
The 1990s (After Sensei's birth):
  • Birth of those a few years younger than Sensei:
    • Niki (Around 1991)
    • Wakana and Osako (Around 1992)
    • Etc
  • Birth of those notably younger than Sensei:
    • Imani
    • Kaori (1997)
    • Etc
  • Sekai likely marries Nozomu, and possibly babysits Sensei, then probably starts molesting Sensei towards the end of the 90s.
Sekai seemed to play peekaboo with Sensei:
View attachment 3769569 View attachment 3769570 View attachment 3769571 Sekai - "It's one we played when you were little."
Sensei Narrator- "STOP PLAYING WITH ME"
Sekai - "It's like you haven't grown a day."
(Chapter 3's 'いないいない。。。ばあ!' Main Event)
  • Sekai probably becomes Sensei's Mother figure, and Teacher.
  • Sensei's father isn't mentioned, but is probably dead by this time. His mother, Saki, might be alive considering Ami still mentions her, but it's not clear.
  • Sensei may have became friends with Niki by now.
Niki and Sensei met at a playground as kids:
View attachment 3769623 View attachment 3769624 View attachment 3769625 View attachment 3769626 Sensei - "A playground?"
Niki - "That's how this all started, after all."
- "Just...two kids who met by chance one day."
- "This is where it all began."
(Chapter 3's Niki 'What It Takes to Move Forward' Event)
2000s:
  • Early 2000s:
    • Sara gets abused by her father, loses her virginity at 13, and probably meets and fucks Sana's father/Sara's high school teacher. Probably has Sana's brother around this time.
    • Sensei basically lives at Niki's house and has likely formed a Girlfriend-like relationship with Sekai. They "fall in love" with eachother.
    • Sekai promises to never leave Sensei.
An example of Sara's childhood:
View attachment 3769653 View attachment 3769652 Narrator - "When she was younger she believed in God."
- "It wasn't until the fifth time her father beat her that she'd given up that belief. And while it could have lasted longer had he not chipped her tooth that night, she was happy to finally be rid of divinity."
(Chapter 4's 'Miserably Ever After' Main Event)
Niki noting Sensei basically lived at her house:
View attachment 3769670 Niki - "We grew up together. Shit, you basically lived at my house."
(Chapter 2's Niki 'Like it's Any Other Day' Event)
Sekai's promise:
View attachment 3769681 View attachment 3769682 View attachment 3769683 Sensei - "You promise?..."
- "You'll really never leave me?..."
Sekai - "Of course."
(Chapter 3's 'Mother May I' Main Event)
  • Mid 2000s:
    • Sekai gets pregnant and has Ami. (Around 2004)
    • Majority of the girls have been born by now. (Karin (2nd year) should have been born around 2003 and Rin (skipped ahead) around 2006 or 2005)
    • Sara's boyfriend/teacher has abandoned her by now. Leaving her to take care of her son by herself, and she was probably pregnant with Sana. Sana is born around 2005. Sara should be around 17/18.
    • Yuki was raped while unconscious, knocked up, and had Yumi around this time. (2004/5)
    • Niki and Sensei have probably had their first kiss by now. Plus hands stuff.
  • Late 2000s
    • Rin was probably sent to an orphanage by now. (Not sure when Rika and Rie adopts her but it's after this point)
    • 3 year old Noriko starts following around and admiring Sensei. By the time she's 6, she probably catches Niki and Sensei fooling around, at some point.
    • Niki and Sensei officially date (dated for 5 years, so it probably started around 2007)
Niki and Noriko note Niki dated Sensei for 5 years:
View attachment 3770271 View attachment 3770275 Niki - "So you can dump me after five years and leave me to rot but you can't even fork over an actual apology."
(Chapter 2's Niki 'Like it's Any Other Day' Event)

Noriko - "Oh, no. I saw him all the time. He dated my sister Niki for five years and was coming over to hang out with her even before that."
(Chapter 2's Noriko 'New Shoes' Event)
2010s (shit goes to shit):
  • Saki (Sensei's mother) is surely dead by now.
  • 6 year old Noriko is seemingly tutored by Sensei, and likely "falls for" him. (Around 2010/11)
  • Around this time, the Wizards are born. Chinami and Tsukasa.
  • 6 year old Maya is likely already "fucked up" and homeless, by now. Presumably due to a relative.
  • Accident happens around 2012 (8 years ago):
    • Sekai breaks her promise by dying.
    • 7 year old Ami watches her parents die. Her mother being torn to shreds.
    • 22/23 year old Sensei sees everything and tries to save Sekai by tearing strips of metal from her body.
    • Some of Sekai's organs are still functional and 15 year old Kaori was presumably in a wreck around this time, perhaps being saved by Sekai's functional organs.
    • Yuki and Yumi likely presumed that Kaori was dead like her parents, around this time.
Niki implies it's been 8 Years since she lost contact with Sensei:
View attachment 3770016 Niki - "You can keep whatever you've done these last eight years to yourself. I don't want to know."
(Chapter 2's Niki 'Like it's Any Other Day' Event)
Ami was said to have been 7 when she lost her parents:
View attachment 3770059 Sensei Narrator - "The only thing is that I can't personally confirm if it's the same type of tantrum she'd throw when she was really little because her parents didn't die until she was seven."
(Chapter 2's Ami 'Heaven for Human Blood' Event)
Ami also watched her parents die:
View attachment 3770070 Ami - "You probably don't realize this because your parents are still alive, but it isn't very fun watching them die."
(Chapter 3's 'The Way it Scatters' Main Event)
  • Months after the Accident:
    • Sensei and Ami somewhat recover enough to function. (Ami probably "falls for" him)
    • Sensei ghosts/dumps Niki.
    • He then continues to tutor Noriko.
    • He takes in and tutors Maya who he has met by this time. (Maya likely "falls for" him)
    • Sensei and Maya have likely formed a sexual relationship by now. (Sensei presumably "falls for" Maya)
    • Ami and Sensei probably moved to their current place to start over, around this time.
Maya and Noriko were apparently being tutored within months of Sensei ghosting Niki:
View attachment 3770076 View attachment 3770077 Noriko - "Wanna know what he does with my sister when they're alone?"
Maya - "They haven't been 'alone' for months. She's a non-factor. And also, no. Because I would like to keep my lunch inside of my body."
(Chapter 4's Noriko 'Rivals (Taco Tuesday)' Event)
  • Ami has more or less started "raising" Sensei by now. Cleaning, cooking, preparing the bath, etc, for him.
  • Chika's and Chinami's father abandons them at some point, (if he was ever around) leaving their mother Chiaki to figure things out.
  • Io is presumably molested by her mother, and has been taking meds since she was 8 years old. She is presumably sent to live with her Aunt.
  • Miku's parents are murdered in front of her, leaving her covered in their blood and traumatized. At some point, she is taken in by Maki and Makoto.
  • Molly's mother has likely killed herself by now.
  • Rin is likely going to therapy for her depression by now, and possibly skipped ahead in school around this time.
  • Tsuneyo's mother is likely no longer in the picture by now, and she may have been adopted by her father who looks nothing like her.
  • Uta has likely got involved with a pedo by now, and at some point, her family finds out, and her brother tries to kill the stalker then ends up incarcerated.
  • 8 year old Yasu predicts the world ending (presumably referring to the accident). Gets taken advantage of by her doctor.
  • Yumi's mother has likely abandoned her, by now.
  • Around 10 year old Ayane gets rich due to her father, her family falls apart, and her mother abandons her soon after Ayane turns 11.
    • Ayane has befriended Ami in elementary school by now, and starts spending most of her time around Ami, and Sensei, who she's "fallen in love" with after breaking down in front of him over her mother.
  • Around 10 year old Nodoka publishes her first book. Presumably is taking care of her mother who can't function, by now. Probably also befriended Futaba around this time.
  • Chika's and Chinami's mother dies, Chika struggles, then likely finds work, gets held back, and probably meets the likes of Yumi and Rin around this time.
  • Sensei and Maya suddenly ghost Noriko, and Sensei stops tutoring around 2016.
Noriko implies it's been almost 5 years since the tutoring:
View attachment 3769837 View attachment 3769838 Maya - "That's why we're still arguing about this fucking bullshit...however many years it's been later."
Noriko - "Almost five...but it feels a hell of a lot longer."
(Chapter 2's 'Goodnight' Main Event)
  • Post Tutoring/2016:
    • Maya becomes a Shrine maiden.
    • Maya and Ami become best friends in middle school.
    • Sana's brother gets murdered, Sara mostly blocks it out, and Sana becomes quiet and meets Ayane around this time.
    • Ami, Ayane, Maya, and Sana become friends.
    • Futaba seems to have developed bulimia by now.
    • Nodoka and Futaba have become close friends by now.
    • Rin and Futaba become like sisters.
    • Chika, Chinami, and Yumi have become like a found family.
    • Nodoka and Otoha become friends.
    • Touka is abandoned by tutor after tutor for some reason.
    • Noriko has begun her search for Sensei and almost finds him in the Old District once.
    • Niki had became suicidal, wasted most of her 20s on Sensei, then gets scouted and becomes an Idol.
    • Most marriages and relationships have been formed, by now.
    • Sensei becomes a Teacher.
    • Uta is sent to live with her grandpa in Kumon-mi, who slowly dies. Probably becomes a Maid around this time.
    • Uta and Io have likely became close friends by now, after thinking eachother were boys.
    • Kirin had likely lost to Ayane at a Science Fair, by now, which created her grudge against her. They had also probably became "friends" by this point.
    • Kirin has also likely became friends with Miku, by now.
    • Etc
  • The Space War happens around 2017, and the majority of men are C̶u̶l̶l̶e̶d̶ sent to space. (May be related to the end of tutoring, and Sensei and Maya ghosting Noriko, but it's not clear)
Haruka implies the space war is around three years old, since that's how long her husband has been gone:
View attachment 3769982 View attachment 3769983 View attachment 3769984 Haruka - "Apart from them, it's probably been...three or four years since anyone else came over?"
(Chapter 1's 'Milk, Eggs, and Water' Main Event)

Sensei - "How long has he been away, if you don't mind me asking?"
Haruka - "Three years, I think."
(Chapter 1's Haruka 'Invisible Worm' Event)
2020 (The Present, technically):
  • It's revealed it's 2020 in Chapter 3.
By Long Maya:
View attachment 3770101 Long Maya - "The date is December 28, 2020. The weather exists. And I have yet to scrub your semen out of my roach-holder."
(Chapter 3's 'Untitled' Main Event)
Uta:
View attachment 3770105 Uta - "In 2020? How would I keep in touch with my parents? Carrier pigeon?"
(Chapter 3's Uta 'Whore' Event)
And Molly:
View attachment 3770106 Molly - "Oh...right. I forgot straight people still exist in 2020. My bad."
(Chapter 4's Tsuneyo 'Soothsayer' Event)
Etc.
  • Sensei becomes the Teacher for all the girls on the first floor.
  • Yumi bullies others, especially Futaba, and ends up getting creepy detentions and stalked by Sensei.
Yumi and creepy Sensei:
View attachment 3770122 View attachment 3770119 Yumi - "You think I just up and forgot about all those fucking creepy ass detentions?! Get real!"
(Chapter 1's Yumi 'Five Million Dollars' Event)
- "Shit, dude. You even tracked me down at the arcade a few times and made it so I can't even chill there anymore."
(Chapter 1's 'Not Even Me' Main Event)
  • Futaba and Makoto begin to admire him. (Probably crush on him)
  • Maya and Sensei seemingly have secret meetings on the roof.
  • Ami, Ayane, Futaba, Maya, Molly, Rin, and Sana, join/make the Manga Club.
  • Sensei becomes the Manga Club's adviser.
  • Months into the School Year, the Resets happened.
  • Tsuneyo's father gets sick and she has to go to school around this time.
Tsuneyo had only been going to school for weeks, after her father got sick, which seems to be around when the game starts:
View attachment 3770199 View attachment 3770226 View attachment 3770224 Tsuneyo - "I have only been coming here for several weeks."
- "I was homeschooled until recently."
- "But my father has become sick and now I must rely on Ms. Watabe."
(Chapter 1's 'Tsuneyo Tojo, Stand-up Comedian' Main Event)
  • Presumably millions of years and hundreds of thousands of iterations of Sensei and the girls occur.
Long Maya implies their show has been "on the air" for millions of years:
View attachment 3770157 Long Maya - "I'd like to take another moment to thank our guest for sharing his thoughts with us- and our sponsors for keeping this show on the air for several million years now."
('Good boy' Happy Event)
Maya implies there's been hundreds of thousands of Sensei's:
View attachment 3770167 Maya - "I mean...Would you be able to handle the memories of hundreds of thousands of lifetimes if they were to all rush in at once?"
(Chapter 1's Maya 'Takoyaki' Event)
And implies each new Sensei reformats the girls:
View attachment 3770181 View attachment 3770177 Maya - "What you were witnessing in those moments were their memories being rewritten."
- "What you were experiencing in watching those girls adapt to you was a type of reformatting."
(Chapter 2's Maya 'Now More Than Ever' Event)
  • Game starts around here.
  • Kaori also got out of the hospital at some point.
  • Himawari/The Shapeshifter was presumably created at some point.
May have missed some things. This game is huge.
Click to expand...
There are some uncertainity I'd like to ask:

1. Do you think Sekai started to molest Akira before or after he met with Niki and gradually built up relationship with him?

2. Both Yui and Saki were inferred to die of diabetes in Second Sun, which is reasonable considering their diet habit in Nothing Is Beautiful, if not treated merely as a joke.

3. I somehow believe that Kaori had a car accident too to parallel with Sekai. But where did it mention "Kaori was saved by Sekai's functional organs"?

4. "Molly's mother has likely killed herself by now" I recall that Molly has said that her mother was already died but where did she stated explicately that she committed suicide?

5. Chika had found a job before she met with Yumi?

6. Tsuneyo was adopted? I remember her mentioning that her mother was Egyptian but I failed to recall if her father adopted her.

7. "Maya and Sensei seemingly have secret meetings on the roof." Can you elaborate on it?

Fire Lord Zuko said:
Omfg! I just had the craziest revelation just now! Remember that post that confirmed Tsubasa was more important than we give her credit for? Well I'm pretty sure she's literally the narrator at the end of the first Beach Vacation. Just look:

View attachment 3768351 View attachment 3768352 View attachment 3768353 View attachment 3768354 View attachment 3768355 View attachment 3768356 Tsubasa Narrator (?) - "What do you believe in?"
- "What's your favorite food?"
- "What kind of music do you like?"
- "I have so many questions for you!"
- "WATCH ME GROW, AS IF I AM A TREE!"
- "And cut me down the second you no longer have a use for me."

Event name: "See You in the Morning" (Chapter 1 Main Event)

View attachment 3768345 View attachment 3768346 View attachment 3768347 View attachment 3768348 View attachment 3768349 Tsubasa - "Which is why I like you. But that's enough about me and my points of view - why don't you tell me a little about yourself?"
- "What do you believe in?"
- "What's your favorite food?"
- "What kind of music do you like?"
- "I have so many questions for you."

Event name: "Playing God" (Tsubasa Chapter 3 Character Event)

The fact she repeats the same questions? The tree reference just a few sentences later (which may or may not be about the sakura at her manor)? At the very least, this is worth looking into. Assuming no one has already pointed this out.
Click to expand...
Moonflare said:
well, fuck. First of all, congratulations on figuring that out. But the repercussions of Tsubasa being the narrator for "see you in the morning" would be astounding (cause that's an entire event that I went through thinking about Tsubasa narrating and it was odd, to say the least, cause there's a lot of stuff there - like the narrator addressing Rin and having her hear the clocks for instance). Well, the name of the Tsubasa event is "playing god" - which could be a nod to her "playing it" instead of being it, and Akira makes a comparison between her and Nodoka (another character that is suspected of hearing the world itself).

I think it's more likely that the narrator for "see you in the morning" is also related to the world itself. Maybe both Nodoka and Tsubasa can hear it, and as Akira puts it, each of them have a different approach to it. One wants to break everything, the other wants to guide them in a better path. Both are tugging the strings though, through information/insight of what they're capable of hearing.

Now, who could be narrating it that would be heard by Tsubasa/related to the tree I have no idea either.
Click to expand...
Great catch. Given the identical wording, I think we have to assume that either Tsubasa is the narrator or is very closely connected to whoever is.

I actually think Tsubasa fits really well with what we know about the (first) beach narrator. As I posted previously, the stuff the narrator says about the tree indicates that they want to become a god or at least godlike.


Earlier in the event, the narrator indicates that they are unhappy with the "God god" who made the world. They want their own world where they can do what they want, which includes helping their loved ones.

The narrator also seems to have empathy for the girls, which I think rules out Sekai/Pareidolia/The World Itself.

All of that seems very consistent with what we know about Tsubasa's motivations, wanting to have the power to manipulate people for benevolent reasons. In "Playing God" she even states that she wants to fill the role of a god who isn't doing their job.



Prior to the beach vacation, the "Cursded Birds" event opens with a monologue that I originally thought was just Sensei, but it actually makes a lot of sense that it's introducing Tsubasa as a new narrator. This is how the event opens:
The opening line is exactly the same as the game's first event ("Every Day I Grow Some More"). However, this time there is a different "first thing" that the narrator doesn't understand, so it's almost certainly a different narrator. I think the repeat of Narrator #1's opening line is meant to indicate a Narrator #2 is now introducing themselves. Also note that the narrator is describing the difference between childhood and adulthood, which implies they have a fair bit of experience with being an adult.

After that, the narrator starts talking about manipulation, which they seem to view as something that helps people
And the monologue closes with an indictment of "God god", which I think is the only time outside of the beach vacation that a narrator uses that term in Chapter 1.
So in summary: possibly a new narrator, is/was an adult, views manipulation as a tool for good, and uses the same language as the beach narrator. Tsubasa seems like a perfect fit.


As for how Tsubasa is able to act as a narrator, I suspect it has something to do with the wishing well (or if Tsubasa isn't the narrator, that's how they're connected).
The beach narrator wants Sensei to throw himself into the wishing well.
The last things that the Xoanon shows us in "Mother's Milk" is the Tsukioka manor sakura tree.
The Xoanon calls Sensei a puppet and says that others want to use him for purposes that the Xoanon agrees with. This could just be the gods, but Tsubasa has explicitly referred to Sensei as her puppet.




The beach narrator tells Sensei he can see more with his eyes closed, and the Xoanon says his eyes are closed to avoid being blinded.


Makoto says the same thing about seeing with your eyes closed in "Bluejay", and there's a good chance that she enters the wishing well since she gets Sensei's eyes. She says it before the suicide, however. Maybe she already has a wishing well connection from doing the same thing in previous resets, I'm not sure.

Edit: Oh and I forgot to mention, the beach narrator talks a lot about ticking clocks (and Rin starts hearing them). The room with clocks might be in the wishing well.
